Measured on the live chips: border-radius 9999px; box 45.2 x 43.8 px; data-state=on background oklab(0.925644 0.0094459 0.0291917/0.83872) and border rgb(198,180,159) BYTE-IDENTICAL to data-state=off; min-block-size auto. Label overhang: 11 of 27 tiles, label 33.2 px over 26.7 px of painted capsule at the label baseline = 6.6 px each. Visible in shots/safari-{desktop,mobile}-{light,dark}/gradient.png, both schemes.
defects.mechanism: Producer packaging defect — a component stylesheet built but never wired into either published CSS entry — surfacing in the consumer as a silently degraded variant.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, Easing row 1. Tiles render as beige circles with labels floating outside them; the pressed tile has no pressed fill. Confirmed by the four committed Safari captures and by the computed-style measurements above.
defects.proposedCure: FOLD-BANK ON GLASS — do NOT patch locally. The cure is one line in the producer: add @import "./glass/glass-chip.css"; to dist/styles/glass.css (or styles/index.css) so the Chip/Badge stylesheet actually ships. Relay on the glass BH inbox against our existing mark M3 (INBOX I-9 / D58, a glass BJ born-RED row) and carry it into the mega-tranche fold as glass-owned. A local .specimen-tile { border-radius: var(--radius-card) } would re-implement producer CSS in a consumer to hide a producer defect — exactly the masking fallback MT-F014 and standing edict 2 forbid — and would survive the glass fix as dead per-instance override.

defects.defect: The component overrides the producer Chip's shape="cell" recipe per-instance from the consumer — re-declaring display, flex-direction, gap and padding on the glass root element — violating standing edict 5 four times in eight lines. It is also causally load-bearing: the local padding + min-width make the box square, which is what turns C-03's orphaned 9999px radius into a full circle rather than a stadium.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170 sets display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:0.125rem; padding:0.3125rem 0.375rem 0.25rem; min-width:2.75rem on the Chip root. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/chip-DFZQr6rV.js already sets shape=cell to 'glass-chip--cell flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro'. Measured resulting box 45.2 x 43.8 px (square) with border-radius 9999px; min-block-size is 'auto' (min-width set, min-height not).
defects.mechanism: Design-system inversion — consumer-side per-instance restyling of a producer root, instead of a producer variant/token, so the seat's density law lives nowhere reusable and fights the producer's own recipe.
defects.reproduction: Read EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170 against chip-DFZQr6rV.js's cell variant string; then getComputedStyle on any [data-specimen] chip in the live page shows padding '5px 6px 4px' and min-inline-size '44px' — the seat's values, not the producer's.
defects.proposedCure: The specimen density is a Chip SIZE, not a demo override. Request a size="xs" rung (or a --chip-cell-density token on shape="cell") from glass-ui, relay it on the BH inbox alongside the M3 orphan, and delete all four declarations here. One producer change then serves this strip, the keyframes T.E6 gallery this was transposed from, and every future micro-cell seat.

defects.defect: A 27-way single-select gallery is exposed to assistive tech as 27 independent aria-pressed toggle buttons — no radio semantics, no roving tabindex, no arrow keys, and the family grouping is aria-hidden so it is invisible to AT. Ahead of them sits the FadingScroll port: tabindex="0" with role=null and aria-label=null, a focusable with no role and no name, because the component labels the inner div instead of passing glass's ariaLabel prop.
defects.evidence: Measured on the open row: 30 focusables; chip role null; chip aria-pressed 'true'/'false'; port { tabindex:'0', role:null, ariaLabel:null }; group label 'Easing curve specimens' present on .strip-row. Playwright AX dump (test-results/oracles-o17-easing-composi-24ab6-...-desktop-smoke/error-context.md:59+) shows a flat group with 27 sibling `button ... [pressed]` nodes, no radiogroup, no per-family structure. glass exposes the prop at dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js:78-92 (role='region' only when ariaLabel/ariaLabelledby given; tabindex="0" hardcoded). Component sites: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:84 (FadingScroll without aria-label), :89 (label on the inner div), :96 (family eyebrow aria-hidden), :98-107 (Chip mode="selectable"). The REPORT's namelessButtons probe filters button,[role=button] (capture.mjs:102-105), so this focusable div is structurally invisible to the audit matrix.
defects.mechanism: Widget-role mismatch — mutually exclusive selection implemented with independent toggle primitives — compounded by an unlabelled producer scroll container inheriting a hardcoded tab stop.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, Easing row 1 open; evaluate getComputedStyle/attributes as above, or read the committed Playwright AX dump. Tabbing from the ramp strip requires 28 keystrokes to clear the strip, the first landing on a roleless unnamed div.
defects.proposedCure: Pass :aria-label="'Easing curve specimens'" to <FadingScroll> (the producer prop exists — use it) and move selection to radio semantics: mode="selectable" Chips inside a reka-ui RadioGroup gives roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, aria-checked and the 1-of-N announcement for free. If glass has no Chip radio rung, that is a glass request on the BH inbox, not a demo hand-roll. Name each tile from its visible label plus its family so the family IA stops being aria-hidden-only.

defects.defect: WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name violation on the `steps` tile: the accessible name is 'steps' while the visible label reads 'n = 4', so a speech-input user saying the visible text cannot activate the control.
defects.evidence: Measured across all 27 tiles: labelInName = [{ acc: 'steps', vis: 'n = 4' }]. Sites: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:105 (:aria-label="tile.id") and easingCatalogue.ts:187 (stepsTile('steps', 'n = 4', 4, 'jump-end')). Visible in the Playwright AX dump as `button "steps": n = 4`.
defects.mechanism: Accessible name minted from a parallel identity string rather than composed from the rendered label, so the two can drift silently.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient Easing row 1 and inspect [data-specimen="steps"]: aria-label='steps', .tile-label text 'n = 4'.
defects.proposedCure: Compose the name from what is rendered rather than from a second source — e.g. name each tile `${fam.family} ${tile.label}` (which also repairs the AT-invisible family grouping from C-05 in the same stroke), or drop aria-label entirely and let the visible label plus an sr-only family prefix compose the name.

defects.defect: The keep-in-view watch's SELECTION arm is intermittent: pressing an off-port tile sometimes fails to scroll it into view, while the REVEAL arm (collapse + re-expand) works reliably. The component's docblock promises both.
defects.evidence: Trial A (fresh load, press [data-specimen="step-end"]): initialScrollLeft 0; after press +1.2 s scrollLeft still 0, tile at x 1673.1-1717.1 against port 237-673, visible false. Then collapse+reopen: scrollLeft 1044, tile at 629.1-673.1, visible true. Trial B (same action, Element.prototype.scrollBy instrumented): exactly one call { fn:'scrollBy', cls:'fading-scroll fading-scrol', args:{left:1044.109375, behavior:'smooth'} } at t=2068, trace 140ms->60.5, 280->645, 420->902, 560->1000, 700->1038, 840->1044, settles 1044. Selection did change in both trials (trial A's later reveal scrolled to step-end's position). Site: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:50-80.
defects.mechanism: HYPOTHESIS (explicitly labelled): the watch is default flush:'pre', so its callback runs BEFORE the component re-renders and its nextTick promise races the parent's own patch for that tick; when the patch lands in a later flush the measurement reads pre-layout geometry and dx computes to 0, silently skipping the scroll at :71 `if (dx !== 0)`.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, Easing row 1 open, press the last tile [data-specimen="step-end"] and sample port.scrollLeft for ~1.4 s. Observed failing once and succeeding once across two clean trials — the BEHAVIOUR is reproduced, the MECHANISM is a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: Stop racing the scheduler: put { flush: 'post' } on the watch so the callback runs after the DOM patch, and delete the nextTick wrapper (and its void-swallowed promise) outright — the measurement then always reads settled geometry. One line removed, one option added.

defects.defect: One complete 27-Chip specimen strip is mounted per gradient interval and never unmounted (v-show, not v-if), so all but one strip is permanently invisible dead DOM, each carrying its own matchMedia listener, ResizeObserver, scroll listener and watcher.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:161 places <EasingSpecimenStrip> inside v-for="row in specimenRows"; the containing panel (:144) and accordion are v-show. Measured with the default two-stop gradient: stripInstances 1, chipsInDom 27. So S stops mount (S-1) x 27 Chips of which (S-2) x 27 are permanently invisible — a five-stop gradient mounts 108 Chips and 108 SVG paths to show 27. Per-instance listeners: useMediaQuery at EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:47; FadingScroll's scroll listener + ResizeObserver + coalesced rAF at dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js:34-45. The catalogue is a module constant (easingCatalogue.ts:198) — nothing varies per interval. The strip's own comment at :40 concedes it: 'sibling rows mount hidden twins of every data-specimen id'.
defects.mechanism: Invariant content duplicated per collection item — a module-constant gallery instantiated inside a v-for it does not depend on — forcing a DOM-scoping workaround (rowEl.querySelector) that exists only because of the duplication.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/gradient and count: document.querySelectorAll('[data-specimen]').length === 27 with one interval; read GradientEasingEditor.vue:161 for the linear relation to interval count.
defects.proposedCure: The accordion has exactly one open row at a time (openInterval: ref<number|null>, GradientEasingEditor.vue:61). Hoist ONE strip out of the v-for and render it for the open interval only. The hidden twins, the rowEl scoping workaround, the N listener sets and the (S-2) x 27 dead nodes all disappear together.

defects.defect: The component's gates are vacuous and the one live oracle over its bench is red. The only unit coverage asserts SPECIMEN_TILES.length > 20 and that no glyph contains 'NaN' — both stay green with six presets dropped (C-02) and three pane-destroying tiles (C-01). There is no component test at all, and e2e oracle o17 — which does press the lethal tile — is currently 3/3 failing.
defects.evidence: test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:55-58. Pasted run: `VJS_E2E_PORT=8191 VJS_E2E_PERF_PORT=8192 npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line` -> `3 failed` (O-17 zero letterbox — desktop; — 390; O-17 composition: stamps, dot rest, one-literal, mint law). The oracle presses [data-specimen='ease-out-back'] at :117 and :189. Honest attribution: all three die EARLIER, at discloseAuthoring (:50-52, #easing-authoring-0 svg[role='img'] never appears) — an EasingAuthoringStage failure, not the strip's; the consequence for this component is that nothing gates it in CI.
defects.mechanism: Gate written against cardinality and string-shape rather than against behaviour or contract, so it cannot distinguish a correct catalogue from a lossy or lethal one.
defects.reproduction: Named mutations that keep the unit test green: (1) delete "circ" and "expo" from FAMILY_ORDER — 21 tiles, still > 20, no NaN, six more curves silently vanish from the product; (2) change glyphPath(fn, samples = 48) to samples = 1 — every portrait collapses to 'M 0.000 1.000 L 1.000 0.000', no 'NaN', count unchanged, every sparkline in the gallery becomes identical. Both pass today.
defects.proposedCure: Repair O-17 first (it is the standing oracle), then replace the cardinality assertions with contract assertions that cannot be satisfied vacuously: (a) every tile in SPECIMEN_TILES, sampled over [0,1], must round-trip through serializeIntervalRamp without throwing; (b) the set of SPECIMEN_TILES ids must equal Object.keys(bezierPresets) union the steps ids. Both fail today; both would have caught C-01 and C-02 at authoring time.

defects.defect: The exported literal minters and the glyph painter carry no arity or domain guard, and bezierLiteral's signature (readonly number[]) does not encode the 4-tuple its body assumes.
defects.evidence: Measured by direct call in the live page: bezierLiteral([0.1, 0.2]) -> 'cubic-bezier(0.1, 0.2, undefined, undefined)'; stepsLiteral(-3, 'jump-end') -> 'steps(-3, jump-end)'; glyphPath(fn, 0) -> 'M NaN NaN'. Sites: easingCatalogue.ts:48-51 (bezierLiteral), :54-56 (stepsLiteral), :66-74 (glyphPath).
defects.mechanism: Partial function published with a total signature — the type admits inputs the body cannot serve, and the failure mode is a silently invalid CSS string rather than an error.
defects.reproduction: In the live page: import the module via /@fs/... and call the three functions with the arguments above. Not reachable from the shipped call sites (the catalogue always passes a 4-tuple, n in {1,4}, and the default 48 samples), hence INFO.
defects.proposedCure: Type the arity so the hole closes at compile time: bezierLiteral(quad: BezierPoints) — the glass BezierPoints type is already imported at easingCatalogue.ts:32 — and give stepsLiteral's count and glyphPath's samples positive-integer types. The 'undefined' and NaN cases then become type errors rather than runtime strings.

defects.defect: The keep-in-view watch's source getter returns a fresh array literal on every evaluation, so Vue's hasChanged gate is always true and the callback runs regardless of whether either prop actually moved — defeating the change detection the getter is written to express.
defects.evidence: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:50-51: watch(() => [selectedId, visible] as const, ...). A new array is never Object.is-equal to its predecessor.
defects.mechanism: Reference-identity change gate applied to a freshly allocated aggregate — the comparison can never report 'unchanged'.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a code-reading finding; the callback is currently idempotent and guards on !visible || selectedId === null, so no user-visible symptom exists today.
defects.proposedCure: Use the idiomatic multi-source form, which compares element-wise and costs nothing: watch([() => selectedId, () => visible], () => { ... }, { immediate: true, flush: 'post' }) — folding in the C-07 flush fix at the same site.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue` (area demo/workbenches), including the composables it instantiates and the children it wires.
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context seat), matching the explicit declaration at spawn. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — deleting the numbers inside a colour function in the CSS box (leaving `oklch()`) throws a TypeError out of `onParseCSS`, which Vue routes to the pane `ErrorBoundary`; the ENTIRE Gradient workbench unmounts behind an error card and recovery remounts a fresh model, so every stop, position, authored easing curve and setting is destroyed silently. Reproduced live twice from a clean load, with the pane's corpse pasted (`handlesAfter: 0`, `editorStillThere: false`, `verdict: null`).
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — but the following brief-named hazards were checked and are genuinely ABSENT, each with positive evidence: (1) PRM-RAF — `grep -rn "requestAnimationFrame" demo/workbenches/gradient/` returns exactly two hits, both one-shot rAFs in `easing/EasingAuthoringStage.vue:58,65`; no loop, gated or ungated, exists in this component or its composables. (2) WebGL/eager canvas — no WebGL, canvas or context anywhere in the subtree. (3) `ValueUnit` nesting — `grep -rn "ValueUnit" demo/workbenches/gradient/` → no matches. (4) `defineModel` stale read AT THIS LEVEL — `selectedStopId` is not bound by `GradientPane.vue:25`, so Vue's `useModel` takes the local-value branch and writes are synchronous here (the child's parent-bound `selectedId` is the armed one, already filed by the prior seat). (5) oklch→HSV hue drift — not applicable; this tree never round-trips through HSV. (6) reka slider pointer-capture leak — `demo/ui/slider/index.ts` re-exports glass-ui's `Slider` wholesale, no demo-side re-implementation to leak. (7) Type safety — `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0, zero output; every type-only import is `import type` (`verbatimModuleSyntax` clean). (8) Edicts 1/4/6 — 279 lines over four composables and three children; `Slider`, `DockControl`, `writeClipboard`, `EasingPicker` all come from `@mkbabb/glass-ui`; the scoped block holds one paint contract and deletes no keyframes.

defects.defect: An ordinary edit in the CSS box (`oklch()` — the state you get by selecting the channel values and pressing Delete) destroys the entire Gradient pane and silently reseeds the model to defaults.
defects.evidence:
GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108 (`onParseCSS`, no try); demo/color-picker/App.vue:50 + ErrorBoundary.vue:59-69. Live run, pasted: {"step0":{"handles":2,"easingReadout":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"},"afterMain":"This panel hit an unexpected error.

Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')

Try again","handlesAfter":0,"verdict":null,"editorStillThere":false}. Headless: `npx vite-node probes/visualizer-probe.ts` → `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue) → THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` (same for rgb()/color()). Screenshot: evidence/gradient-pane-destroyed-by-oklch-empty.png shows the auto-recovered pane holding the DEFAULT gradient, not the user's.
defects.mechanism: `applyCSS` is documented model-or-reject but is not total: `parseGradientCSS`→`isColorToken`→`parseCssColor` throws on an empty colour function (src/css/grammar.ts:181 non-null assertion). The throw crosses an emitted-handler boundary, so Vue's callWithErrorHandling routes it to onErrorCaptured; the boundary unmounts the subtree. Because `useGradientModel()` is instantiated INSIDE the component (line 32), the model's lifetime is the view's lifetime — any throw is a data-loss event.
defects.reproduction: goto http://localhost:9000/, wait 1.2s, set location.hash='#/gradient' in-page, wait for [role=textbox][aria-label='Gradient CSS'], select all its text, insertText 'linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)', dispatch input, wait 2000ms → main.innerText is the error card, 0 stop handles, no verdict.
defects.proposedCure: Two independent moves: (a) make the grammar total — return a failure for an empty component list in src/css/grammar.ts rather than asserting slash[0] (a try/catch in the pane would be a masking fallback, edict 2); (b) transpose the ownership — hoist `useGradientModel()` to a route-scoped provide ABOVE the ErrorBoundary so the model outlives its view and 'Try again' remounts a view over surviving state.

defects.defect: Adding or removing a stop anywhere but the end silently re-hosts every authored easing curve one slot to the left and drops the last one.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:90-92 (`onAddStop`) and :143 (`@remove`) wire into useGradientModel.ts:89-100, a watcher keyed on `stops.value.length` alone. My run: `before: 0,50,100 → cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) | steps(4, jump-end)` / `after: 0,25,50,100 → cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) | steps(4, jump-end) | cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)` — 'interval that was 50→100 (steps) now covers: 25→50'.
defects.mechanism: Intervals are a parallel array keyed by index and reconciled by length; an insert at index k shifts the meaning of every interval ≥ k without touching the array, and appends a fresh linear at the end. Remove truncates the tail, not the removed adjacency.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P2. In the UI: author steps(4) on the second easing row, click the rail at 25% to add a stop, watch the steps curve jump to the first quarter and the second half revert to linear.
defects.proposedCure: Stop modelling an adjacency relation as a parallel array. Carry the outgoing curve on the stop that begins the interval (one array, no synchronisation possible), or key intervals by the id pair `${a.id}:${b.id}` so an insert must SPLIT an interval explicitly.

defects.defect: The drag handler drops the ordering invariant: the component emits CSS its own parser rejects, the rail paints a clamped slab, and its own `colorAtPosition` ghost then previews a colour that matches neither.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:94-96 writes a raw position; useGradientModel.ts:118 (addStop) sorts and gradientParse.ts:284-290 rejects. My run: `positions: 70,50,100` → `simpleCSS: linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 70%, lime 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` → `re-parse of the app's own output: REJECTED — stop positions must be non-decreasing`; `rail sub-stop positions: 33 samples, 16 DECREASING steps`; `ghost/add color the visualizer mints at 60%: oklch(0.75 0.15 145)` (the first stop's colour, via the line-67 short-circuit).
defects.mechanism: Three owners, three policies for one invariant. `colorAtPosition` (lines 64-88) additionally assumes a sorted list: with list[0] at 70%, every query ≤70 short-circuits to the first stop's colour while the rail at that position paints a CSS-clamped slab from a different pair. The line-87 `throw` is unreachable dead code (any walk from below to above the query must cross upward through a covering ascending pair).
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node .../probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P3. Live: add a stop at 50%, drag the 0% handle right past it, then type any character in the CSS box — the editor goes destructive-red with a reason unrelated to the user's edit.
defects.proposedCure: Make ordering a property of the type, not of an array: one `setStopPosition(id, pos)` writer that returns the re-sorted model and re-keys intervals (see C-5), with `stops` exposed readonly to the view.

defects.defect: The Copy button copies a completely different string from the one displayed beneath it, and discards the producer's failure result.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:254 (`<DockControl title="Copy CSS" @click="copyCSS">`) sits directly above :258 (`<GradientCodeEditor :model-value="simpleCSS">`), while :127-129 is `await writeClipboard(coalescedCSS.value)`. Measured: `editor shows (simpleCSS, 74 chars)` vs `clipboard gets (coalescedCSS, 1363 chars)`, `identical? false`. glass-ui contract: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:32-37 — 'Returns the discriminated result … const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)'.
defects.mechanism: Two different serialisations of the model are bound to the same visual affordance; the authored literals P2-15 exists to preserve are destroyed in the copied form. The awaited CopyResult is dropped, so a denied permission / insecure context / Safari gesture rule fails with no surface at all — the dock action (usePaneRouter.ts:209) is equally silent.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node .../probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P5.
defects.proposedCure: Copy what is on screen (`simpleCSS`) — or show what is copied. Then adopt the producer's `useClipboard({resetMs})` (already used by the sibling GradientEasingEditor.vue:94) so both success and failure have a surface, with an aria-live confirmation.

defects.defect: `resetGradient` does not reset: authored easing curves and the selection survive a 'Reset to defaults'.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:118-125 pokes six fields but never touches `intervals`; useGradientModel.ts:89-100 only re-seeds intervals when the stop COUNT changes, and reset replaces 2 stops with 2 stops. My run: `before reset: interval[0].css=steps(4, jump-end)` / `after reset: interval[0].css=steps(4, jump-end)` / `RESET RESTORED THE linear SEED? false`, with the pasted coalesced output showing the 4-band staircase.
defects.mechanism: Reset is expressed as a sequence of field assignments over a model whose invariants are maintained elsewhere; the one field it cannot reach by assignment is the one reconciled by a length-keyed watcher. `selectedStopId` is also left pointing at a destroyed stop id.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node .../probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P1. Live: pick the `steps` specimen tile, then fire the dock's Reset action — the gradient stays a staircase.
defects.proposedCure: Reset = adopt the seed model. Keep the seed literal in one place inside `useGradientModel` and expose `resetModel()` that swaps the whole GradientModelState atomically, exactly as `applyCSS` already does for a parsed model.

defects.defect: `seedFromPalette` is a silent no-op for the common case, seeds from an arbitrary palette, and admits unvalidated colour strings that then throw inside a render computed.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:110-116. My run: `coalescedCSS computed THREW PickerColorError: Invalid CSS color` after `setStopsFromColors(["#112233","not-a-color"])`; `1-colour seed → stops=1 intervals=0` (an illegal model below the ≥2-stop invariant both removeStop and parseGradientCSS enforce). Dock wiring: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:210, description 'Seed gradient stops from a saved palette.'
defects.mechanism: `if (!pm) return` and `if (colors && colors.length >= 2)` swallow both failure modes with no verdict, while the CSS door next to it has a whole verdict surface. `savedPalettes.value[0]` is a positional guess, not a user choice. `setStopsFromColors` stores strings verbatim; validation happens later, inside computeds consumed by the template — so a malformed palette row becomes a render-time throw (the C-1 pane-destruction path from a second door).
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node .../probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P8. Live: with no saved palettes, fire the dock's 'Seed from palette' — nothing happens and nothing is said.
defects.proposedCure: Make the seed a real command over a user-chosen palette that validates through the library oracle at the boundary and returns the same `{ok:false, reason}` shape the CSS path returns — one failure surface for both doors — and move the ≥2-stop invariant into `setStopsFromColors` where it can be enforced.

defects.defect: There is no keyboard path to add a stop, and the rail carries no role or name.
defects.evidence: Live measurement: `barRole: {role: null, tabindex: null, aria: null}`; handles are 20×20 with no tabindex override. The only add gesture is a pointer click on the bar (GradientStopEditor.vue:101-110 → @add → GradientVisualizer.vue:90). The three dock actions (usePaneRouter.ts:208-210) are Reset / Copy CSS / Seed — no add. REPORT.json /#/gradient smallTapTargets includes 'Gradient stop at 0%' and 'Gradient stop at 100%' at 20×20 in all four Safari matrices.
defects.mechanism: The rail is a bare div with pointer handlers; the handles are buttons with a name but no slider semantics, so arrow-key nudges only mutate the accessible NAME (not reliably announced) and creation is pointer-only. WCAG 2.1.1 (A) and 2.5.8 (AA).
defects.reproduction: Live evaluate on /#/gradient: `document.querySelector('[data-testid="gradient-stop-bar"]')` → role/tabindex/aria-label all null; tab through the pane — no control adds a stop.
defects.proposedCure: Give the rail the semantics it already behaves as: handles become role=slider with aria-valuemin/max/now/valuetext and aria-orientation, the rail becomes a named role=group, and one keyboard-reachable 'Add stop' control exists (which also serves the touch user who cannot hover to see the ghost).

defects.defect: The Copy CSS control has no accessible name — it is the single nameless button the visual audit counts on /#/gradient in all four Safari matrices.
defects.evidence: Live: `copyBtnName: {ariaLabel: null, title: 'Copy CSS', text: ''}` with `copyBtnHtml` showing `<button … title="Copy CSS">`. REPORT.md namelessButtons: /#/gradient = 1 on desktop-light, desktop-dark, mobile-light, mobile-dark (gradient is one of only two routes still showing one on mobile). The audit's rule is visual/capture.mjs:102-105 (aria-label || aria-labelledby || textContent).
defects.mechanism: GradientVisualizer.vue:254 passes only `title`; the icon child (`<Copy class="w-5 h-5"/>`) contributes no text. `title` is an accname last resort — unspoken by several SR/browser pairings and invisible on touch. The sibling GradientEasingEditor.vue:181 shows the house idiom is :aria-label. WCAG 4.1.2.
defects.reproduction: Live evaluate on /#/gradient: `[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b => !(b.getAttribute('aria-label')||b.getAttribute('aria-labelledby')||b.textContent.trim()))` → the Copy CSS DockControl.
defects.proposedCure: aria-label="Copy gradient CSS" on the control, aria-hidden on the icon, and (with C-2) a live-region confirmation so the result is perceivable too.

defects.defect: The Direction slider is a dead control whenever Type is Radial, and the authored angle is silently destroyed by the radial round-trip.
defects.evidence: `npx vite-node probes/direction-probe.ts`: 'radial 0deg vs 270deg identical? true' (linear/conic false). Round-trip: 'simpleCSS shown for radial @137deg: radial-gradient(red 0%, blue 100%)' → 're-parsed direction: 0 (authored 137)'. Also 'linear-gradient(-90deg,…) → direction=-90' and '1e6deg → 1000000' against a :min=0 :max=360 slider.
defects.mechanism: `direction` is modelled as a field of every gradient, but serializeCoalescedGradient/serializeGradient only emit it for linear and conic (useGradientCSS.ts:151-155, 285-289). The slider stays enabled with a live degree readout that has no effect; and because the editor re-parses the displayed text on a 500ms debounce, the dropped field comes back as 0 — silent data loss with no verdict.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/direction-probe.ts. Live: set 137°, switch Type→Radial, type a character in the CSS box, switch back to Linear — the angle is 0.
defects.proposedCure: Direction belongs to the linear and conic geometries, not to 'a gradient'. Model a discriminated GradientGeometry so the control's presence is derived from the type and the serializer cannot drop a field the model claims to hold.

defects.defect: The Hue interpolation control is inert in four of the nine spaces the Space control offers, with no disabled state and no explanation.
defects.evidence: `npx vite-node probes/visualizer-probe.ts` → P4, over the exact INTERPOLATION_SPACES list (color-space-meta.ts:26-36): oklch false, lch false, hsl false, oklab TRUE, lab TRUE, rgb TRUE, xyz TRUE (true = shorter and longer produce byte-identical output).
defects.mechanism: HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS is rendered unconditionally (GradientVisualizer.vue:198-210); hue arcs only exist in polar spaces. The control accepts input, drives a full recompute of the whole gradient chain, and produces an identical result.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node .../probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P4. Live: choose Space=RGB and flip Hue between Shorter and Longer — nothing changes.
defects.proposedCure: Derive availability from the selected space — PICKER_CHANNELS[space] already carries `hue?: true` per channel, so the fact lives in the library — and disable-with-reason instead of silently ignoring.

defects.defect: No gate that runs can see this component: no unit test imports the SFC, and the only behavioural gate (e2e) is RED and absent from CI.
defects.evidence: `npx vitest run test/gradient-parse.test.ts test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts` → 22 passed (parser + serializers only). `grep -rln "GradientVisualizer" test/ demo/test/` → only gradient-v4-consume.test.ts, and it imports .../GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue, not the SFC. `grep -rn "playwright|test:e2e" .github/workflows/*.yml` → no output; ci.yml:32-37 runs lint, two vue-tsc projects, build, `npm test`. e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:57,112 assert a role=img 'Perceived-space plate' that no longer exists (`grep -rn "Perceived-space" demo/` → no matches).
defects.mechanism: The gate surface is drawn around pure functions (parser, serializers) while every defect in this report lives in the component's wiring, its exposed actions and its templates.
defects.reproduction: Exact vacuous mutation: replace the whole file with `<script setup lang="ts">defineExpose({resetGradient(){},copyCSS(){},seedFromPalette(){}});</script><template><div/></template>` — lint, both vue-tsc projects, build and `npm test` all stay green and CI reports success.
defects.proposedCure: One jsdom component test that mounts GradientVisualizer and asserts the three exposed actions plus the two catastrophic inputs (`oklch()` typed into the editor; a cross-drag), and a CI job that runs `test:e2e` after the stale plate assertions are retired.

defects.defect: A single coarse `modelState` makes every field change repaint everything; ≥3 of the 4 recomputed products are provably invariant to the field that triggered them, and 4.26 KB of inline style is rewritten per tick.
defects.evidence: `npx vite-node probes/cost-probe.ts` (V8, excludes Vue patch/style recalc/raster): 2 stops → coalescedCSS 0.085 ms, railRampCSS 0.073, specimenRows 0.031, openIntervalRamp 0.075, ONE tick 0.265 ms, doubled by the bar+handle emit 0.530 ms; 8 stops → 0.449 / 0.899 ms. Live DOM: tile inline style 2131 chars, rail 2129. Invariance: 'railRampCSS same at 90deg and 271deg? true', 'specimenRows … true', 'intervalRamp … true'.
defects.mechanism: useGradientModel.ts:102-109 exposes one computed object; every consumer depends on all of it, so a Direction tick invalidates the rail ramp, the specimen rows and the open interval ramp — all provably direction-invariant. `colorToCss` emits full float precision (measured live: `oklch(74.687500147402% 0.150937499558 148.749998231174deg)`), so each tick also rewrites two ~2.1 KB inline gradient strings.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/cost-probe.ts
defects.proposedCure: Split the state by what varies: geometry (type, direction) feeds only the render tile; ramp facts (stops, intervals, space, hue) feed the rail and the specimen rows. Two computeds instead of one, and round the serialised channels at the single serialisation boundary.

defects.defect: Selection is a public model that leads nowhere and is written twice; a stop's colour cannot be edited at all, and the pane's injected session colour is dropped on the floor.
defects.evidence: GradientVisualizer.vue:51 declares `defineModel('selectedStopId')`, but GradientPane.vue:25 binds nothing and no code in the file reads it; lines 140 and 144 write the same fact through both `v-model:selected-id` and `@select`. `grep -rn "updateStop" demo/` → one call site, GradientVisualizer.vue:95, with `{position}` only. GradientPane.vue:8 injects cssColorOpaque from CSS_COLOR_KEY and never uses it.
defects.mechanism: A two-way model prop with no consumer plus a redundant emit is dual-path indirection (edict 2/3); and the selection has no consequence because no colour-edit path was ever wired, so `updateStop`'s cssColor branch is dead API.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static: grep for updateStop call sites and for selectedStopId bindings.
defects.proposedCure: Either give selection its consequence — the selected stop becomes the pane's edit target through the existing EDIT_TARGET_KEY / CSS_COLOR_KEY contract — or delete the model, the @select emit and the dead injection. Today the code pays for both and delivers neither.

defects.defect: Section headings collide with the pane's own heading level, and the render tile's accessible name describes the widget rather than the gradient.
defects.evidence: PaneHeader.vue:21 renders the pane title as <h3>; GradientVisualizer.vue:149, :241, :253 render 'Interpolation', 'Easing', 'CSS' as <h3> as well. REPORT.json counts.h1 = 0 on every route. Tile: lines 221-222, role=img with aria-label='Gradient render with type and direction applied'.
defects.mechanism: Same-level headings make the sections siblings of the pane title in the accessibility tree, so heading navigation yields a flat list with no containment (WCAG 1.3.1). The role=img promises a described picture but the name states no type, angle or colour — all of which the component already holds.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static: read PaneHeader.vue:21 against GradientVisualizer.vue:149/241/253.
defects.proposedCure: One heading-level contract for panes (pane title h2, sections h3) expressed in PaneHeader and consumed, not restated; and compose the tile's name from the live model (`${type} gradient at ${direction}°, ${n} stops from X to Y`).

defects.defect: The parse verdict's aria-live region is created at the same moment as its content, so the component's only failure channel may never be announced.
defects.evidence:
GradientCodeEditor.vue:107-114 — `

{{ parseVerdict }}

`; the verdict value is owned by GradientVisualizer.vue:100/107.
defects.mechanism: Several SR/browser pairings (VoiceOver+Safari, this project's stated matrix) only announce mutations of a live region already present in the accessibility tree; a region inserted pre-populated is commonly missed. WCAG 4.1.3.
defects.reproduction: NONE — mechanism/spec-level; not driven with a screen reader in this pass.
defects.proposedCure: Render the status region unconditionally (empty, no visual cost) and write text into it, so every verdict is a mutation of a live region rather than an insertion.

defects.defect: The model is transiently illegal after every stop change: n stops with n-2 intervals until an async watcher flushes.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:89-100 (async watch). My run, reading synchronously right after addStop: 'THREW Gradient interval 3 is missing' (useGradientCSS.ts:189).
defects.mechanism: Stops and intervals are updated by two separate writes separated by the scheduler. Vue's pre-flush ordering keeps today's render path safe, so this is luck about scheduler ordering rather than an invariant: any flush:'sync' watcher, watchSyncEffect, or handler that reads a computed in the same tick as an add lands in the illegal window.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node .../probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P6, the 'synchronous read straight after addStop' line.
defects.proposedCure: Stops and intervals change in ONE assignment (the shape `applyCSS` already uses) — or, better, stop having two arrays at all (see C-5).

defects.defect: Four smaller sharp edges: two id counters with one shape, three unchecked AcceptableValue casts, an uncancelled debounce, an unbounded module-level easing cache.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:66-69 and gradientParse.ts:31-34 both mint `stop-${++n}-${Date.now().toString(36)}` from independent counters (my run: model-minted stop-26/27 vs parser-minted stop-4/5 in the same millisecond suffix). GradientVisualizer.vue:164/181/198 cast `AcceptableValue` (which includes null/undefined) to the domain type with no runtime guard. demo/shared/utils.ts:36 provides `debounce.cancel`, GradientCodeEditor.vue:55 never wires it to unmount. useGradientCSS.ts:69 `resolvedEasingCache` has no eviction.
defects.mechanism: Uniqueness by coincidence (two counters must never collide within one millisecond), type-safety by assertion rather than by guard, and a timer that can fire into an unmounted tree — where, with C-1 in play, no boundary is left to catch the throw.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the casts and the id collision (hypotheses — probability, not demonstration); the counters and the missing cancel are shown by the pasted P9 output and by grep.
defects.proposedCure: One id source (or a monotonic counter with no time component); parse the select value through the domain's own vocabulary instead of asserting; call `debouncedParse.cancel()` in onBeforeUnmount.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — the tier explicitly declared at spawn; not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — MixConfigBar's headline feature (the T-17 library-sampled preview ramps, ~45% of the 173-line file and the reason 3 of its 9 imports exist) has never rendered once in the shipped app. demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:168 passes tag="button" to glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which has NO `tag` prop and renders an aria-hidden, inline-`pointer-events:none` <span>, swallowing @click and aria-label. All 13 add-a-color affordances on /#/mix are pointer-dead, keyboard-dead and AT-invisible, so `operandColors` is permanently [] and every <PreviewRamp v-if> is false (measured live: dataStops 0, previewRamps 0, `<!--v-if-->` in the rendered #description). Six gates are green over the dead feature: vue-tsc cannot see it (a fallthrough attr is never a type error), test/preview-chips.test.ts tests the sampler not the consume path, and e2e o14-preview-truth.spec.ts is itself broken by the same defect (2 failed, and its one surviving leg — "honest absence: <2 operands → NO chip" — now passes vacuously and forever).
result.negativeProof: Verified sound, recorded as evidence rather than silence: (1) The published-surface consume is correct — MixConfigBar.vue:12 imports HueInterpolationMethod from `@mkbabb/value.js/color`, a real key in package.json#exports backed by src/subpaths/color.ts:8, resolved by an alias set GENERATED from package.json#exports at vite.config.ts:37-50 so it cannot drift; zero `@src/*` and zero deep-src/ imports in the subject's transitive demo graph — a real consumer could write every value.js import in this file verbatim. (2) verbatimModuleSyntax honoured — all four type-only imports (lines 12,13,14,15) carry `import type`, the six value imports do not. (3) Vue 3.5 idioms correct — reactive props destructure with default at 25-45, typed defineEmits at 76-81, no defineModel stale-read hazard (emit-based), no template refs needed. (4) The file's own "the sampling costs nothing at rest" claim (lines 19-22) is TRUE and was verified, not assumed: Vue computeds are lazy and the only readers live inside the unmounted SelectContent subtree. (5) Visual/a11y clean — REPORT.md:123,138,153,168 give /#/mix overflowX 0 / pageErr 0 / consoleErr 0 across all four Safari matrices; I read shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png and shots/safari-mobile-dark/mix.png and the grid-cols-2 pair holds at 390px without wrap or clip in both schemes; REPORT.json probe.a11y.smallTapTargets on /#/mix are all dock/picker chrome ("Switch to slug", "Generate new slug", "Cancel", "L/A/B/ALPHA channel") — none belong to MixConfigBar, whose three SelectTriggers all carry aria-labels and appear in the live a11y tree. The disabled low-contrast Mix verb visible in both screenshots is L-1's symptom, not a styling defect.

defects.defect: MixConfigBar's entire T-17 preview-ramp feature is unreachable dead code, because the mix workbench passes a `tag` prop that glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot does not have. The primitive renders an aria-hidden, inline-`pointer-events:none` <span> and discards @click/aria-label as fallthrough attrs, so every add-a-color affordance on /#/mix is dead → canMix can never be true in colors mode and operandColors is permanently [].
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:168 (`tag="button"`), :171 (aria-label), :173 (@click). glass-ui prop set at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts = {color, variant?, animate?, cycleDuration?, range?, seed?} — no `tag`. LIVE at http://localhost:9000/#/mix: {pointerEvents:"none", ariaHidden:"true", hasAriaLabel:false, tabIndex:-1, swatchesBefore:5, swatchesAfter:5} after el.click(); pointer-events:none is an INLINE style (matched stylesheet rules with pointer-events:none = []). After opening "From palettes": {totalSwatches:13, pointerDeadSwatches:13, realAddColorButtons:0}. Subject's own Space menu open: {options:9, dataStops:0, previewRamps:0, firstOptionHTML:"...Perceptual, hue-preserving"}. E2E: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o14-preview-truth.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "T-17"` → `Error: locator.click: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded. - waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Add current color to the mix' }) > 355 | await addSlot.click();` … `2 failed / 1 passed (43.6s)`. Repo-wide: 7 `tag="button"` sites in MixSourceSelector.vue:168,:215, GenerateControls.vue:203, SwatchHoverMenu.vue:17,:32, CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:98, plus ~14 `tag="div"` sites. Dead code in subject: MixConfigBar.vue:19-23, 47-74, 104-115, 127-137.
defects.mechanism: legacy prop survived a major design-system upgrade (glass-ui 7.0.0 adoption at W44 migrated CSS/variants, never audited props); Vue never type-errors on an extra attr passed to a component, so vue-tsc is silent by construction; the demo assumed a `tag`-polymorphic interactive primitive that glass-ui ships as decorative-only
defects.reproduction: 1. http://localhost:9000/#/mix (fresh load). 2. devtools: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost')).pointerEvents → "none"; document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost').tagName → "SPAN"; .getAttribute('aria-hidden') → "true"; .hasAttribute('aria-label') → false. 3. document.querySelectorAll('button[aria-label^="Add color"]').length → 0. 4. click the Color space Select: document.querySelectorAll('[data-stops]').length → 0.
defects.proposedCure: Do not polymorph across the design-system boundary — wrap. The interactive seat is a real <button> (or glass-ui's existing Chip/Button primitive) that CONTAINS a decorative <WatercolorDot aria-hidden>: semantics and focus on the element the demo owns, paint on the glass-ui primitive. Delete all 21 `tag=` props repo-wide. Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox regardless — a primitive that silently swallows @click + aria-label while stamping aria-hidden is a footgun for every consumer; if a tag-polymorphic swatch is genuinely wanted it is a glass-ui SwatchButton variant (edict 4), not a demo prop.

defects.defect: The mix domain module is homed in a sibling FEATURE tree with zero consumers there, and half of it is library-grade color math the published library lacks. demo/palettes/mix.ts exports mixColorSequence — N-ary weighted mixing over readonly AnyColor[] with zero demo/DOM/Vue coupling — while @mkbabb/value.js/color ships only binary mixColors.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:14 imports LeftoverStrategy from ../../palettes/mix. Complete consumer set: `grep -rn 'palettes/mix"' demo` → demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:14 and demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:21 — ZERO consumers inside demo/palettes/ (a feature tree: PalettesPane.vue, BrowsePane.vue, admin/, api/, browser/). Library surface: `grep -rn "export function mixColors" src/` → src/color/operations.ts:83 (binary only). demo/palettes/mix.ts:40-67 = mixColorSequence(colors, space, hueMethod, weights). Same argument for demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts:52-88 whose only non-library deps are the 3-line wrappers color-utils.ts:11-13 and :23-25. The subject's own header at MixConfigBar.vue:16-17 documents this exact cure being applied to the OTHER vocabulary ("S.W5-6 · F16 … no more cross-feature reach") and not to this one.
defects.mechanism: inverted ownership / cross-feature reach — a module lives where it was first written rather than where its consumers are, and library-grade pure math is trapped in the demo so the dogfood proof knows something the published API does not
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'palettes/mix"' demo --include='*.vue' --include='*.ts'  → 2 hits, both under demo/workbenches/mix/, none under demo/palettes/
defects.proposedCure: Promote the pure math UP and the palette shape ACROSS. Add mixColorSequence(colors, {space, hue, weights}) and sampleColorRamp(colors, {space, hue, k}) to src/color/operations.ts beside mixColors, exported via src/subpaths/color.ts. demo/palettes/mix.ts then collapses to its palette-shaped remainder (LeftoverStrategy, getColorAtIndex, mixPalettes) and moves to demo/workbenches/mix/mix.ts beside its only two consumers; color-chips/sample.ts becomes a ~10-line serialization shim. Net: library gains two reusable operations, demo loses a cross-feature edge.

defects.defect: A second, diverged implementation of this exact component. GradientVisualizer.vue:179-210 is the same Space+Hue Select pair over the same vocabulary with the same trigger height, #description lane, caption class and AcceptableValue cast idiom as MixConfigBar.vue:97-140 — but the T-17 preview-chip grammar landed only in the Mix copy.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:97-140 vs GradientVisualizer.vue:179-210 (identical structure; gradient rows carry no <PreviewRamp>). MEASURED live at /#/gradient with the Space menu open — gradient always carries ≥2 stops so the sampler would return non-null: {openItems:9, labels:["OKLCh Perceptual, hue-preserving","OKLab Perceptual, smooth",…,"XYZ CIE absolute"], dataStopsInDoc:0}. The divergence is documented as pending and never landed: demo/color-session/color-chips/index.ts — "Lane D wires MixConfigBar + AuroraPane; … the GradientVisualizer consume through Lane G's queue."
defects.mechanism: duplicated concept with no single owner; a handoff note standing in for a structural invariant, so the two copies drift apart the moment one is enhanced
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → click [aria-label="Interpolation space"] → document.querySelectorAll('[data-stops]').length → 0 (vs. the same grammar's 13 rows specified in MixConfigBar.vue:107,129)
defects.proposedCure: One component owns the interpolation-config pair. Extract demo/color-session/InterpolationConfig.vue beside the existing ColorSpaceSelector.vue precedent, with v-model:space / v-model:hue / :operands and chips included by construction; Mix and Gradient both consume it. MixConfigBar shrinks 173 → ~60 lines (leftover-strategy row + the Mix verb) and stops being two things. This subsumes L-5 entirely.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 19 pure re-export alias barrels over @mkbabb/glass-ui with no added surface, and the tree runs a live dual path — two specifiers for one design system, split with no rule.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:3-9 and :10 import through the barrels. All 19 demo/ui/*/index.ts files total 20 non-comment lines; demo/ui/select/index.ts in full: `export { Select, SelectTrigger, SelectItem, SelectValue, SelectContent, SelectGroup, SelectLabel, SelectSeparator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. Measured split: barrel-import sites 90, direct `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui..."` sites 119. Arbitrary boundary — Select/Button/Card via barrel; WatercolorDot, DockControl, SearchBar, SegmentedTabs, GlassDock, Chip, FadingScroll direct. Within one feature: MixSourceSelector.vue:7 direct (@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot), MixPane.vue:12 direct (writeClipboard), MixPane.vue:3 via barrel (Card). demo/ui/alert/index.ts:1-9 self-documents as a converted shim.
defects.mechanism: back-compat shim outliving its migration — the barrels once held local shadcn implementations, were converted to re-exports, and were never deleted; violates edict 2 (no aliases/dual paths) and edict 3 (no wrapper layers that add nothing)
defects.reproduction: for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do grep -vc '^\s*\(//\|/\*\|\*\|$\)' "$f"; done  → 19 files, 20 non-comment lines, every one a bare re-export
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely; rewrite the 90 import sites to the specifier they already resolve to (@mkbabb/glass-ui, or the subpath where one exists — demo/ui/input/index.ts is the only barrel hiding one, @mkbabb/glass-ui/forms). Mechanical, one commit, and it removes the last place in the tree where "which import path is correct?" has two answers.

defects.defect: A three-hop re-export chain keeps INTERPOLATION_SPACES / HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS reachable by three distinct specifiers, kept alive — in the source's own words — so consumers can keep their import path.
defects.evidence: Canonical home demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:26,38 → re-exported at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:17 → re-exported again at useGradientModel.ts:21 → consumed at GradientVisualizer.vue:19-20. The subject imports the canonical home directly (MixConfigBar.vue:18). Stated reason, useGradientInterpolation.ts:14-16: "Re-exported here so the gradient tree's own consumers (useGradientModel → visualizer) keep their import path."
defects.mechanism: verbatim back-compat shim — the exact construct edict 2 prohibits; it also makes a MODEL composable a re-export hub for color-space metadata it never touches
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "INTERPOLATION_SPACES" demo --include='*.vue' --include='*.ts'  → the 4-link chain above, with MixConfigBar.vue:18 on the canonical path and GradientVisualizer.vue:19 on the chain's end
defects.proposedCure: Delete both `export { … } from` lines and point GradientVisualizer.vue:19-20 at color-session/color-space-meta — the same one-line import the subject already writes. Subsumed entirely if L-3's cure lands.

defects.defect: MixConfigBar reaches AROUND the design system into glass-ui's own peer dependency for a type, and the borrowed type is strictly wider than glass-ui's real emit — advertising a contract (bigint, objects, null) glass-ui never offers, then laundering it with an unguarded `as PickerSpace`. Root cause is a glass-ui published-surface hole.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:15 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui"`, used at :99, :122, :146. glass-ui's real contract, dist/components/select/Select.vue.d.ts: `"update:modelValue": [value: SelectionValue]`; dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts: `export type SelectionValue = string | number`. reka-ui's is `string | number | bigint | Record<string, any> | null` (node_modules/reka-ui/dist/index3.d.ts:231). The hole, measured: `grep -ln "SelectionValue" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.d.ts` → NO OUTPUT — the alias is named in no published entrypoint; components/select/index.d.ts re-exports SelectProps/SelectEmits/SelectItemProps but not SelectionValue, and glass-ui's exports map (69 subpaths) has no ./components/* wildcard, so the deep path is blocked. Four demo sites reached for reka-ui instead: MixConfigBar.vue:15, GradientVisualizer.vue:28, GenerateControls.vue:33, AuroraPane.vue:25.
defects.mechanism: public-surface hole in the design system forces consumers to reach past it into its transitive dep; the wider type compiles only because a wider handler param is contravariantly assignable — the type system agrees with a false statement
defects.reproduction: grep -ln "SelectionValue" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.d.ts  → no output; node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').exports))" → no ./components/* wildcard
defects.proposedCure: Two-sided. (a) BH relay to glass-ui: one line — `export type { SelectionValue, isSelectionValue }` from components/select/index.ts and the root barrel, so a consumer can name its own Select's model-value type. (b) In the demo, type the handlers (v: SelectionValue) and delete all four reka-ui imports; the demo then touches the design system's transitive deps in exactly zero places. Interim, nameable through the published surface TODAY and honest: SelectProps["modelValue"] — no new dependency edge, no wider lie.

defects.defect: No module owns portal teardown across a route change: opening a glass-ui Select and then hash-navigating leaves `body { pointer-events: none; overflow: hidden }` stuck, bricking every control on the destination route — including the subject's own two Selects and the Mix verb.
defects.evidence: Reproduced live. After /#/gradient → click [aria-label="Interpolation space"] → navigate to /#/mix (hash change, no reload): document.body.getAttribute('style') → "pointer-events: none; overflow: hidden;"; hit-test at the centre of a pane control (add-slot rect x687 y344 48×48) document.elementFromPoint(711,368).tagName → "HTML"; Playwright click fails with `<html> intercepts pointer events`. Hard reload of /#/mix clears it: body style → null, same hit-test → DIV.swatch-row. Isolates the cause to the cross-route overlay.
defects.mechanism: ownership hole — reka-ui's body scroll-lock/pointer guard is applied on Select open and its teardown never runs when the route change unmounts the portal; nothing in demo/shell/ owns "dismiss every portalled overlay on route change", so each pane mounts overlays and nobody unmounts them as a class
defects.reproduction: 1. http://localhost:9000/#/gradient  2. click [aria-label="Interpolation space"]  3. navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/mix (hash route change, no reload)  4. document.body.getAttribute('style') → "pointer-events: none; overflow: hidden;"  — every control on /#/mix now dead. HYPOTHESIS (not measured): the subject's own two Selects strand any route navigated to next by the identical path; only gradient→mix was measured.
defects.proposedCure: One shell-level guard, not a per-pane fix: a router.beforeEach (or a single watch(route) in the app shell) that closes all open overlay state and defensively clears the body lock — one writer, one place. Relay the underlying teardown miss to glass-ui, since the guard is glass-ui's Select / reka's to release.

defects.defect: The leftover-strategy vocabulary is split across two trees and modelled asymmetrically from its own siblings: the type lives in demo/palettes/mix.ts while the labels and a hand-listed, non-exhaustive STRATEGIES array live inline in the SFC — where the sibling space/hue vocabulary got a proper meta module.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:83 `const STRATEGIES: LeftoverStrategy[] = ["discard","repeat","distribute"]` and :85-89 `strategyLabels: Record<LeftoverStrategy,string>`; type at demo/palettes/mix.ts:19. Compare demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:26,38 — {value,label,description} meta for spaces and hues. strategyLabels IS exhaustive-checked (a Record over a union requires every key); STRATEGIES is NOT — it is a hand-restatement TypeScript cannot police.
defects.mechanism: split ownership with one of the two links unenforced — add a fourth strategy to the union and strategyLabels errors loudly while STRATEGIES silently drops the new option from the UI
defects.reproduction: Add a fourth member to LeftoverStrategy at demo/palettes/mix.ts:19 and run typecheck: MixConfigBar.vue:85 errors (missing Record key), MixConfigBar.vue:83 does not — the Select renders 3 of 4 options with no diagnostic.
defects.proposedCure: One LEFTOVER_STRATEGIES: {value;label;description}[] beside the type in the (relocated, per L-2) mix module, with the union DERIVED from it — `type LeftoverStrategy = typeof LEFTOVER_STRATEGIES[number]["value"]` — so the list is the single source and drift is impossible. The SFC then holds zero vocabulary, matching how it already treats spaces and hues.

defects.defect: The chip sampler's cost — 13 rows × 16 stops ≈ 208 mixColors calls per re-evaluation — goes live the moment L-1 is cured, re-running on every pointer-move while a menu is open.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:57-74 builds two Maps over INTERPOLATION_SPACES (9) + HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS (4); RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT = 16 at demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts. NOT currently a defect: the file's claim at :19-22 ("the chips render only while SelectContent is mounted … so the sampling costs nothing at rest") is CORRECT and was verified — Vue computeds are lazy and the only readers live inside the unmounted SelectContent subtree.
defects.mechanism: a latent full cross-product recomputation, currently masked by L-1 keeping operandColors empty and by computed laziness while the menu is closed
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a hypothesis about post-cure behaviour. It cannot be exhibited today because L-1 makes operandColors permanently [] and the ramps never evaluate.
defects.proposedCure: Fold into L-2's cure: sampleColorRamp in the library, memoised on (operands, space, hue), with only the candidate axis re-sampled per row rather than the full 9×4 cross-product.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — matches the seat's explicit declaration; not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: D-1: `data-mix-target` at MixResultDisplay.vue:69 never reaches the DOM. glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot declares `inheritAttrs: false` and re-binds only `class`+`style`, so the convergence anchor the entire mix animation aims at does not exist. mixStage.ts:121-124 therefore always takes its hard-coded fallback and the pigment pool lands ~180-220px above the well. Proven by mounting the real SFC through the live Vite dev server: `document.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-target]').length === 0`, rendered attrs = [data-v-*, aria-hidden, class, data-testid, data-variant, style]. Regression origin: glass-ui 490cc46e (Glass 7 cut, 2026-07-16) removed the `tag` prop + `<slot/>` and added `inheritAttrs:false`; value.js f2c8f565 adopted 7.0.0 without touching a single WatercolorDot call site. Invisible to vue-tsc (verified clean) and to tests (0 unit tests; both e2e specs die at an earlier line).
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Clean sub-areas, each positively checked and recorded in the report: verbatimModuleSyntax compliant; Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure used correctly; no defineModel so no stale-read hazard; zero component-owned rAF/timers/listeners/observers — the feature's one rAF rides glass-ui useRAFLoop with pauseWhenHidden + onBeforeUnmount stop + a PRM complete-immediately fast path; no ValueUnit wrapping, no oklch→HSV roundtrip, no parseCssColor call; no WebGL; 159 lines, not a god module; /#/mix shows 0 page errors, 0 console errors, 0 horizontal overflow, exactly 1 main across all four Safari matrices in REPORT.md:123/138/153/168.)

defects.defect: The convergence anchor `data-mix-target` (MixResultDisplay.vue:69) is never rendered. glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot sets `inheritAttrs: false` and forwards only `class`+`style`, so every non-prop attribute is silently discarded. mixStage.ts:121-124 always takes its `else` fallback and the mix pigment pool lands on a hard-coded guess instead of the well.
defects.evidence: Live mount of the real SFC via /@fs/ through the dev server → {"mixTargetsInProbe": 0, "dotTag": "SPAN", "dotAttrs": ["data-v-292b9032","data-v-0f138735","aria-hidden","class","data-testid","data-variant","style"]}. Mechanism: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js `inheritAttrs: !1` with `c = i(() => n.class), f = i(() => n.style)` only. Fallback: demo/workbenches/mix/MixAnimationCanvas/composables/mixStage.ts:121-124. Measured landing miss on the live /#/mix pane: {"rootClientWidth":356,"rootScrollHeight":785,"fallbackLanding":{"x":178,"y":549.5,"r":28},"approxPlateTopY":769,"deltaY":-219}. Origin: glass-ui 490cc46e (2026-07-16) `git log -S inheritAttrs` sole hit; pre-7 file had `53: tag?: "div"|"button"`, `114: <component`, `215: <slot />` and no inheritAttrs:false. value.js f2c8f565 adopted 7.0.0 with zero WatercolorDot call-site changes.
defects.mechanism: unaudited dependency-major attribute-forwarding contract change; consumer relies on attribute inheritance from an inheritAttrs:false component, with a silent geometric fallback downstream that manufactures a wrong-but-plausible result
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000, then in the page: `const vue = await import('/@id/vue'); const mod = await import('/@fs/<repo>/demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue'); const h=document.createElement('div'); document.body.appendChild(h); vue.createApp(mod.default,{result:{type:'color',css:'oklab(0.6 0.1 0.05)'},ghost:true}).mount(h); h.querySelectorAll('[data-mix-target]').length` → 0
defects.proposedCure: Anchor on markup the component owns: move `data-mix-target` onto the ghost wrapper `<div v-if="ghost" key="well">` at line 63 and size that wrapper to the dot so layoutCenter's offsetWidth/Height read the true box — anchors belong on host DOM, never on a third-party component's attribute-forwarding contract. Then make the missing anchor loud: mixStage.ts:121-124's silent fallback must dev-warn or return null (the caller at useMixingAnimation.ts:149-154 already settles honestly on null). A fallback that fabricates a plausible wrong geometry is worse than none.

defects.defect: Three dead `tag="div"` props and a dropped `:title` on WatercolorDot. `tag` was a real prop pre-Glass-7 and is now noise; the dropped `:title` means a palette result exposes no readable colour value at all — the swatches are aria-hidden/pointer-events:none with no title, and the gradient strip is aria-hidden role=presentation.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:67,81,100 (`tag="div"`), :103 (`:title="color.css"`), :109-116 (aria-hidden strip). Rendered attr list from the live mount contains neither `tag` nor `title`. Pre-7 glass-ui `git show 490cc46e^:src/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue` line 53 `tag?: "div" | "button"`, line 64 default "div". `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → clean, exit 0 (no diagnostic exists for a dead fallthrough attr).
defects.mechanism: same inheritAttrs:false drop as D-1, plus removed props left in place after a major bump — call sites express intent the runtime cannot honour
defects.reproduction: Same live mount as D-1; inspect the swatch element's attributes — no `title`, no `tag`. Then `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → no errors, proving the type system cannot catch it.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three `tag="div"`. Render each palette swatch's value as real text (the single-colour branch already does this at :85-87) rather than relying on a tooltip that is unreachable by touch and keyboard anyway. If a titled/labelled swatch register is wanted, it belongs in glass-ui (edict 4) and must be relayed to the active glass-ui inbox — never re-minted in demo/.

defects.defect: The scoped `.mix-plate { transition: opacity … }` rule overrides the design-system `.vj-morph-enter-active` on the same element (scoped attribute raises specificity to 0,2,0 vs 0,1,0) and the `transition` shorthand resets transition-property to `opacity` alone — deleting the morph's transform spring and max-height channels.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:152-154 vs demo/styles/animations.css:104-109. Measured in the live cascade: with the scope attribute → {"transitionProperty":"opacity","transitionDuration":"0.2s"}; identical classes without it → {"transitionProperty":"opacity, transform, max-height","transitionDuration":"0.2s, 0.44s, 0.3s"}. The plate is the transitioned root (MixPane.vue:111 wraps MixResultDisplay in <Transition name="vj-morph">).
defects.mechanism: per-instance scoped shorthand out-specifying a design-system transition class on the same element — an animation deleted as a side effect of a local override (owner edicts 5 and 6)
defects.reproduction: In the page: create `<div class="mix-plate vj-morph-enter-active" data-v-0f138735>` and a control without the data-v attribute, append both, read getComputedStyle().transitionProperty → "opacity" vs "opacity, transform, max-height".
defects.proposedCure: Ghost-dimming is a family behaviour, not a plate quirk. Move it into the vj-morph/ghost family in demo/styles/animations.css as a token-driven modifier so exactly one `transition` declaration governs the element, and delete the <style scoped> block entirely.

defects.defect: The async result is silent to assistive tech and the three action buttons carry no accessible name beyond `title`. No aria-live/role=status anywhere; the 'Copied!' confirmation is a title swap on an already-focused button.
defects.evidence: Live mount: {"D_ariaLive": 0, "namelessByHarnessRule": 3} and each button {"text":"","title":"Copy color|Save to palettes|Reset","ariaLabel":null,"w":28,"h":28}. The repo's own rule at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/capture.mjs:102-105 counts a button nameless unless it has aria-label/aria-labelledby/text. Sibling MixSourceSelector.vue:169 and :251 use aria-label correctly. Result arrives ~900ms after the click (mixStage.ts:24 MIX_CONVERGE_MS=900) via MixPane.vue:111-119 with no focus move.
defects.mechanism: async-result surface with no announcement channel; accessible naming delegated to a title attribute that the repo's own harness (and touch users) do not accept
defects.reproduction: Mount MixResultDisplay with a colour result and query `host.querySelectorAll('[aria-live],[role="status"],[role="alert"]').length` → 0; filter buttons by the capture.mjs:102-105 predicate → 3 of 3 nameless.
defects.proposedCure: aria-label on all three DockControls (matching the sibling's convention), plus one `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region in the plate carrying both the settled result value and the copy outcome — one region discharges the silent-result and the unannounceable-confirmation defects together.

defects.defect: Clipboard failure is completely silent and permanent. `copied` collapses useClipboard's 4-state machine to `status === 'success'`, so `failure` renders identically to idle; the library schedules its reset timer only on the success branch, and no `onCopyError` is supplied.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:31-32. dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js: `n.ok ? (a.value="success", l=setTimeout(…, i.resetMs ?? 1500), n) : (a.value="failure", i.onCopyError?.(n.reason), n)` — no reset on failure. Live simulation of a non-secure context (the repo's own LAN-http mobile-testing mode, vite server.host:true): {"titleBefore":"Copy color","titleAfter":"Copy color","anyErrorTextInPlate":false,"liveRegions":0} — nothing changes at all.
defects.mechanism: 4-state status collapsed to a boolean at the consumption site; the error state has no render path and no reporting hook
defects.reproduction: Mount MixResultDisplay with a colour result, then `Object.defineProperty(navigator,'clipboard',{value:undefined,configurable:true})` and click the Copy button — after 300ms the title is unchanged, no error text, no live region.
defects.proposedCure: Render the third state: drive the icon and the new live region off `status` directly instead of collapsing to a boolean at :32, and pass `onCopyError` so the failure reason is reportable. The collapse itself is the defect.

defects.defect: The copy confirmation goes stale across a re-mix and affirms a value that was never copied. MIX_CONVERGE_MS(900) + vj-morph(~200) ≈ 1100ms is shorter than resetMs 1500ms, and the component instance is not remounted, so the check mark survives into the next result.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:31 (resetMs 1500) vs mixStage.ts:24 (MIX_CONVERGE_MS=900) and demo/styles/animations.css:104-109 (--duration-fast). Measured: {"step1_afterCopy":{"title":"Copied!","iconClass":"… lucide-check …"}, "step2_afterReMix_1270ms":{"title":"Copied!","iconClass":"… lucide-check …"}, "step2_plateText":"RESULT oklab(0.3 -0.05 0.09)"} — the plate shows result B while the button still affirms the copy of result A. useClipboard exports `invalidate()` (dist `d()`); MixResultDisplay.vue:31 destructures only {status, copy}.
defects.mechanism: confirmation lifetime bound to a timer instead of to the identity of the thing confirmed
defects.reproduction: Mount MixResultDisplay with a reactive result; click Copy; after 120ms set ghost=true and swap in a new result; after 900ms set ghost=false; read the copy button at ~1270ms — title still 'Copied!', icon still Check, while the plate text is the new colour.
defects.proposedCure: `const { status, copy, invalidate } = useClipboard()` plus `watch(() => result, invalidate)`. Bind the confirmation to the result identity; do not race it against a timer.

defects.defect: Two divergent copy implementations for one user-visible action: the plate button uses useClipboard (with confirmation), while the dock's 'Copy result' action calls MixPane.copyResult which uses writeClipboard with no confirmation. The text-derivation expression is duplicated verbatim in both files.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:42-47 vs MixPane.vue:49-55, wired at demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:222 `handler: () => paneRefs.mix.value?.copyResult?.()`. Identical derivation duplicated: `result.type === "color" ? result.css ?? "" : result.colors?.map((c) => c.css).join(", ") ?? ""`. MixPane.vue:57 defineExpose({clearSelection, startMix, copyResult}).
defects.mechanism: dual code paths for one action (owner edict 2), with a masking optional-call `?.()` on a statically exposed method
defects.reproduction: Read demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:222 and compare MixResultDisplay.vue:43-46 with MixPane.vue:51-53 — same rule, two copies, two primitives, only one of which produces confirmation state in the plate.
defects.proposedCure: One derivation, one primitive. Put `resultToClipboardText(result)` next to `MixResult` in composables/useMixingState.ts (that module owns the result shape) and let a single owner hold the useClipboard scope — either the dock action routes to the plate's handler, or MixPane owns the scope and passes copy/status down. Either is fine; two are not.

defects.defect: An empty palette result renders a plate that says 'Result' and shows nothing: zero swatches, an invalid `linear-gradient(to right, )` that resolves to background-image:none, and three live buttons — Copy copies "" and reports success, Save persists an empty palette.
defects.evidence: Reachable via demo/palettes/mix.ts:117 `if (palettes.length === 0) return []` and :120 `if (resultLength === 0) return []` (fires under the default 'discard' strategy, useMixingState.ts:46) → useMixingState.ts:97 sets {type:'palette', colors: []}. MixResultDisplay.vue:91 guards on `result.colors` (an empty array is truthy). Measured: {"renderedStripPresent":true,"inlineBg":null,"computedBgImage":"none","swatchCount":0,"text":"RESULT"}. Save path: MixPane.vue:44-46.
defects.mechanism: truthiness guard on a collection instead of a length guard; no empty-state branch; actions live when there is nothing to act on
defects.reproduction: Mount MixResultDisplay with `{ result: { type: 'palette', colors: [] } }` → the plate renders the word RESULT, no swatches, a 16px transparent strip (computed background-image 'none'), and three enabled action buttons.
defects.proposedCure: Guard on `result.colors.length > 0`, and give the truly empty result the repo's existing empty-state grammar — MixSourceSelector.vue:240-244 already mounts an eyebrow/message/hint component for 'nothing to mix'. Reuse it (edict 3: no new wrappers). Disable the actions when there is nothing to act on.

defects.defect: `MixResult` is a non-discriminated interface with optional payloads (`css?`, `colors?`), so `{type:'color'}` with no css is type-legal and renders the same blank plate as D-8. This looseness is what forces the four masking `??` fallbacks in the component.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:32-36. Masking fallbacks at MixResultDisplay.vue:37-39 (`?? "var(--muted-foreground)"`) and :44-45 (`?? ""` twice). Measured render for {type:'color'} with no css: {"swatchCount":0,"text":"RESULT"}. Not reachable via startMix today (useMixingState.ts:90 always sets css) — this is the type being looser than the invariant.
defects.mechanism: impossible states left representable, then papered over with fallbacks that convert them into silently wrong renders
defects.reproduction: Mount MixResultDisplay with `{ result: { type: 'color' } }` → blank plate with only the RESULT label and three buttons. (Type-checks clean.)
defects.proposedCure: Make it a real discriminated union — `{ type: "color"; css: string } | { type: "palette"; colors: readonly [PaletteColor, ...PaletteColor[]] }` — which makes the blank plate unrepresentable and deletes all four `??` fallbacks, forcing startMix to decide what an empty palette mix means at the one place that knows.

defects.defect: The palette TransitionGroup keys by array index, which defeats the vj-enter stagger it exists for: Vue patches nodes in place so re-mixing N colours into N different colours plays no enter animation, and the index also drives `seed`, coupling a dot's silhouette to its slot rather than to what it is.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:92-105, `:key="i"` at :99 and `:seed="i === 0 ? 'mix-result' : `mix-result-${i}`"` at :104. The correctly-keyed sibling is MixSourceSelector.vue:129 `:key="swatchKeys[i]"`.
defects.mechanism: positional keys on a keyed-transition list whose identity is the colour, not the slot
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis by inspection of Vue's keyed-patch semantics; the animation-suppression claim is not separately measured. The code citations are exact.
defects.proposedCure: Key on a stable colour identity (`${i}-${color.css}` at minimum, a real id preferably) and derive `seed` from the same identity, so a dot's silhouette follows the colour rather than the position.

defects.defect: The gate is vacuous, and the vacuous mutation is the shipped state. Zero unit tests exist for this component; the only two tests asserting `[data-mix-target]` both fail at an earlier line so that assertion has never been evaluated; and vue-tsc is structurally blind to a dropped fallthrough attribute.
defects.evidence: `grep -rln 'MixResult|MixPane|mix-plate' test/ e2e/` → only e2e/smoke/oracles/o7-card-census.spec.ts (unrelated). e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts:52 and e2e/smoke/safari/mix-flow.spec.ts:40 assert the anchor. Run: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line` → "1 failed … expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed / Locator: getByRole('button', { name: 'Add current color to the mix' }) / element(s) not found / > 42 | await expect(addSlot).toBeVisible();" — dies at line 42, ten lines before the anchor assertion. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → clean, exit 0.
defects.mechanism: the component's central DOM contract has no rendered-DOM assertion at any level; the one e2e that would cover it is masked behind an unrelated earlier failure in the same spec
defects.reproduction: Named vacuous mutation: delete `data-mix-target` from MixResultDisplay.vue:69 entirely. Typecheck stays green (verified), the unit suite stays green (there is none), and both e2e specs are unchanged because they already fail at line 42. That mutation is behaviourally identical to what ships today.
defects.proposedCure: A component test that mounts MixResultDisplay with ghost:true and asserts `wrapper.find('[data-mix-target]').exists()` — an assertion on the rendered DOM contract, not on source text. Repo-wide: every data-* handshake that crosses a component boundary needs this class of test, because the type system provably cannot supply one. Separately, fix the source-selector break so the mix specs stop masking every downstream assertion behind one early failure.

defects.defect: All three DockControl action buttons measure 28x28 px — above the repo harness's 24px bar and WCAG 2.5.8, below WCAG 2.5.5's 44px. `compact` opts out of DockControl's documented '>=44px on coarse via the density clamp'.
