defects.evidence: Live mount: sizes ["28x28","28x28","28x28"]; harness threshold `.filter((m) => m.w < 24 || m.h < 24)` at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/capture.mjs:98. DockControl.vue.d.ts documents the coarse density clamp that `compact` bypasses. MixResultDisplay.vue:121,128,136 all pass `compact`.
defects.mechanism: compact variant bypassing the coarse-pointer density clamp on a touch-reachable surface
defects.reproduction: Mount MixResultDisplay with a colour result and read getBoundingClientRect() on each button → 28x28.
defects.proposedCure: Owner ruling needed on whether `compact` is legitimate on a touch surface; if yes, the clamp should apply to compact too — and that decision belongs in glass-ui's DockControl, not in a demo override.

defects.defect: Redundant configuration and an inconsistent built-in import: `useClipboard({ resetMs: 1500 })` restates the library default, and `TransitionGroup` is imported from vue while `Transition` is left to auto-resolution.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:31 `useClipboard({ resetMs: 1500 })` vs dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js `i.resetMs ?? 1500`. MixResultDisplay.vue:4 `import { computed, TransitionGroup } from "vue"` while `<Transition>` at :60 is unimported. Both are auto-resolved in <script setup>.
defects.mechanism: configuration that says nothing, plus asymmetric handling of two built-ins in the same file
defects.reproduction: NONE — inspection; the citations are exact.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the redundant resetMs argument and the TransitionGroup import; let both built-ins auto-resolve.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m] (1M-context variant), matching the explicit declaration under which this seat was spawned.
result.strongestDefect: L-1: the component's documented raison d'être does not work. `MixResultDisplay.vue:69` publishes the mix convergence's landing anchor as `data-mix-target` on a glass-ui `<WatercolorDot>`, but glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot sets `inheritAttrs:false` and forwards ONLY `$attrs.class`/`$attrs.style` — the attribute never reaches the DOM (per-frame sampling: `everTarget:false` across 700ms of both first-mix and re-mix, and at settle). `mixStage.ts:121` therefore always misses and always takes its invented-point fallback at `:122-124`, landing the pigment pool 251px from the well — 56px from the centre of the Mix button, visible in the screenshot. A stringly-typed DOM contract across a third-party boundary, with a downstream masking fallback that converts the break into plausible-looking motion, under a typecheck gate (`vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0, 0 lines) that is structurally blind to the class.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (The one clean axis worth recording: the `@mkbabb/value.js` public-surface question passes at this component. MixResultDisplay imports the library not at all; its transitive reach is `useMixingState.ts:19` → `import type { HueInterpolationMethod } from "@mkbabb/value.js/color"`, a genuine `package.json#exports` subpath a real consumer could write. No demo→`src/` deep import, no feature→shell or component→boot edge. The T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone holds here; the drift is one hop away in `tsconfig.demo.json` (L-8), not in this file.)

defects.defect: The mix convergence anchor `data-mix-target` (MixResultDisplay.vue:69) never reaches the DOM, because it is stamped on a glass-ui `<WatercolorDot>` that discards all fallthrough attributes. `mixStage.ts:121`'s querySelector always returns null and its masking fallback at :122-124 always fires, so the pigment drops converge on an invented point 251px from the well they are documented to land in.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js — decompiled: `inheritAttrs: !1`, setup reads only `n=useAttrs(); c=computed(()=>n.class); f=computed(()=>n.style)`, root is `createElementBlock("span", {"aria-hidden":"true", class:[c.value,…], "data-testid":…, "data-variant":…, style:[f.value,{…pointerEvents:"none"…}]})`; no `v-bind="$attrs"`. LIVE per-frame DOM sampling on localhost:9000/#/mix (seeded localStorage, palettes mode, 2 palettes, Mix clicked): `"mix1":{"everTarget":false,"last":{"t":701,"target":false,"plate":true,"ghostCls":true}}`, `"settled":{"plate":true,"target":false}`, `"mix2":{"everTarget":false}`. Measured geometry at t≈120ms: rootClientWidth=510, rootScrollHeight=702, fallbackPoint={x:255,y:491.4}, wellCenterLocal={x:61,y:650.5}, missDistancePx=251, mixBtnCenterLocal={x:256,y:547.8}, distToMixBtnPx=56. Screenshot shows the purple pool sitting on the Mix button.
defects.mechanism: Stringly-typed cross-module DOM-attribute port, routed through a third-party component whose attribute-forwarding policy the demo neither controls nor typechecks; compounded by a downstream masking fallback that invents a plausible coordinate instead of failing.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/L-wbmixresult-probe.mjs and .../L-geom.mjs against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000. Both seed localStorage["color-palettes"] with two palettes via addInitScript, switch to Palettes mode, select both, click Mix, and sample `document.querySelector('[data-mix-target]')` per rAF for 700ms.
defects.proposedCure: Transposition, not patch: replace the DOM-attribute side channel with a typed anchor port. New `demo/workbenches/mix/mixAnchors.ts` exporting `MIX_ANCHORS_KEY: InjectionKey<{well: Ref<HTMLElement|null>; sources: Ref<HTMLElement[]>}>`. MixPane provides; MixResultDisplay binds `useTemplateRef("well")` to a plain wrapper div IT owns (never to the glass-ui dot — the dot is a paint, not an anchor); useMixingAnimation injects and passes a real element into `collectStage(target: HTMLElement, sources: HTMLElement[], …)`. Delete the querySelector and the invented-point branch entirely; a missing anchor settles honestly through the path that already exists at useMixingAnimation.ts:148-154. Same fix retires `[data-mix-source]` (mixStage.ts:129).

defects.defect: `tag` is a prop that does not exist on glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot. MixResultDisplay.vue:67, :81, :101 pass `tag="div"`; :103 passes `:title="color.css"`. Both are silently discarded. 21 such call sites across demo/, and the demo typecheck is fully green on all of them.
defects.evidence: `grep -c 'tag' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` → 0. `grep -o 'o("[a-z]*"' …/watercolor-dot.js | sort | uniq -c` → `2 o("span"` / `1 o("svg")` (root is always span). d.ts props are exactly {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}. Live settled plate: dots render as `{"tag":"SPAN","attrs":["data-v-292b9032","data-v-0f138735","aria-hidden","class","data-testid","data-variant","style"]}` ×3 — no `tag`, no `title`. Repo census: 21 WatercolorDot openers passing `tag=` (MixResultDisplay.vue:64,:79,:97 among them; MixResultDisplay.vue:94's `tag="div"` is on TransitionGroup and is CORRECT). Gate: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` → `EXIT=0`, 0 lines of output.
defects.mechanism: Consumer-side ownership of a producer-side render seam with no compile-time contract — Vue treats unknown component attributes as fallthrough attrs, so no gate in this repo can distinguish a live prop from a string appended to nothing.
defects.reproduction: grep -c 'tag' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js  →  0 ; then npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit  →  exit 0. The dead props typecheck.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui-owned under edict 4: restore on WatercolorDot the host seam its sibling primitives already publish (reka `Primitive` `as`/`asChild`, exactly as DockControl exposes), add `v-bind="$attrs"` on the root, and drive `pointer-events` off whether an interactive host was requested. Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox. Demo-side, delete the 21 dead `tag=`/`title=` props rather than leaving them as false documentation — note L-1's cure removes MixResultDisplay's need for a host seam at all.

defects.defect: One concept — "copy the mix result" — has two implementations, two clipboard APIs and two import paths inside a single feature directory. MixResultDisplay.vue:31,42-47 uses `useClipboard` with confirmation state; MixPane.vue:12,49-55 uses `writeClipboard` with none; the `MixResult → string` serialization is written twice, character-identical.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:31 `const { status, copy } = useClipboard({ resetMs: 1500 })` + :42-47 `onCopy`. MixPane.vue:12 `import { writeClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` + :49-55 `copyResult` + :57 `defineExpose({ clearSelection, startMix, copyResult })`. Second path reachable from the shell: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:222 `{ key:"copy", …, handler: () => paneRefs.mix.value?.copyResult?.() }`. Both symbols live in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts, published at `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom` — and the sibling useMixingAnimation.ts:41 already imports `useBreakpoint` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom`.
defects.mechanism: Missing unique semantic ownership: the result→text projection has no home, so each consumer re-derives it; and the feature imports one glass-ui composable from the root barrel and its neighbour from the narrow subpath.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "copyResult" demo/ → MixPane.vue:49, MixPane.vue:57, demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:222. Invoke the palette's "Copy result" command and the plate's copy button: identical intent, different feedback (1500ms check vs nothing).
defects.proposedCure: `mixResultToText(result: MixResult): string` beside the type in a pure `mix.ts`; `useMixingState` owns exactly ONE `useClipboard` and returns `{copyStatus, copyResult}`; the plate renders `copyStatus`; `MixPane.defineExpose` re-exports the same function. One home per concept, one specifier (`@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom`).

defects.defect: The clipboard primitive hands the component a discriminated failure channel and the component throws it away. MixResultDisplay.vue:46 `await copy(text);` discards the `CopyResult`; :32 reads only `status === "success"`, so a `"failure"` renders pixel-identical to idle.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts: `export type CopyResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: CopyFailureReason }`, documented as "Returns the discriminated result … rather than a lossy boolean" and "A failed copy always names its channel"; `UseClipboardOptions.onCopyError` also offered. MixResultDisplay.vue:46 `await copy(text);` (return discarded), :32 `const copied = computed(() => status.value === "success")`.
defects.mechanism: Masking fallback (edict 2) — the library was upgraded to be failure-explicit and the consumer stayed failure-silent; the failure state is representable but unrepresented.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis for the user-visible half. The code path is proven by file:line; the Safari non-gesture clipboard rejection that exercises it was not driven in this session.
defects.proposedCure: `const res = await copy(text); if (!res.ok) …` with a three-state plate affordance (idle / copied / failed), or pass `onCopyError`. This is already the house idiom in the same feature — mixStage.ts:106 does `if (!result.ok) throw new Error(…)` on value.js's Result shape.

defects.defect: `MixResult` is a union that is not discriminated. useMixingState.ts:32-36 declares `{type: "color"|"palette"; css?: string; colors?: PaletteColor[]}`, permitting states the producer never emits and forcing ten `??`/`?.` masking operators and four re-guards across three files.
defects.evidence: useMixingState.ts:32-36. Tax sites: MixResultDisplay.vue:37-39 (2 `??`, incl. `result.css ?? "var(--muted-foreground)"`), :44-45 (2 `??`), :78 and :91 (re-guards `&& result.css` / `&& result.colors`); MixPane.vue:41,:44,:52,:53; useMixingAnimation.ts:78,:81. Producer only ever emits the two valid shapes (useMixingState.ts:90, :97).
defects.mechanism: Impossible states left representable — the type does not encode the machine's invariant, so every consumer re-defends it, and one defence (wellColor's grey fallback) paints a plausible wrong result instead of surfacing a bug.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural. Read useMixingState.ts:32-36 against MixResultDisplay.vue:37-45,:78,:91 and count.
defects.proposedCure: `type MixResult = { kind: "color"; css: string } | { kind: "palette"; colors: PaletteColor[] }`. `v-if="result.kind === 'color'"` narrows; every `??` and every re-guard deletes itself; the ghost sizing ternary at :71 reads the discriminant directly. Fourteen defensive constructs become zero.

defects.defect: Dock primitives used in a plate that has no dock: MixResultDisplay.vue:120-143 builds its action row from `DockControl compact` ×3 + `DockSeparator` inside `.mix-plate`, where `--dock-control-size` does not resolve. Measured hit box is 28×28px — DockControl's own docstring guarantees ≥44px on coarse via the density clamp, a guarantee that only holds inside a dock root.
defects.evidence: Live measurement inside the settled plate: `dockControlSizeToken: "(unset)"`; `actionButtons: [{title:"Copy color",ariaLabel:null,w:28,h:28},{title:"Save to palettes",ariaLabel:null,w:28,h:28},{title:"Reset",ariaLabel:null,w:28,h:28}]`; `separators: 1`. glass-ui dist/components/dock/DockControl.vue.d.ts docstring: "the HIT CELL stays the full `--dock-control-size` (≥44px on coarse via the density clamp) — hit box ≠ paint box". DockSeparator.vue.d.ts resolves its axis via `useOptionalDockContext()` and the `.glass-dock` ancestor class, absent here.
defects.mechanism: A primitive's guarantee lives on its ancestor (the dock root's density clamp and CSS custom properties) rather than on the primitive, so importing it through a published subpath imports the component without its contract.
defects.reproduction: node .../scratchpad/L-geom.mjs — reads `getComputedStyle(plateButton).getPropertyValue("--dock-control-size")` and `getBoundingClientRect()` of the three plate action buttons after a mix settles.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui publishes `./button`, an icon register with no dock dependency — use it; or, better under edict 4, glass-ui moves the ≥44px coarse clamp onto DockControl itself so the guarantee travels with the component rather than with its ancestor. Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox together with L-2.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is a 19-barrel shadow namespace whose every entry is a pure re-export of glass-ui — a legacy alias layer giving two import paths to one design system, with both paths alive in this feature directory.
defects.evidence: `cat demo/ui/card/index.ts` → `export { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. All 19 barrels are the same shape (alert avatar badge button card checkbox collapsible dialog dropdown-menu input label popover radio-group select separator skeleton slider switch tooltip). Dual path in one directory: MixPane.vue:3 `import { Card } from "../../ui/card"` (shim → glass-ui root) vs MixResultDisplay.vue:3 `import { DockControl, DockSeparator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock"` (subpath).
defects.mechanism: Migration shim never retired — edict 2 (no aliases/dual paths) and edict 3 (no contrivance).
defects.reproduction: for d in demo/ui/*/; do head -c 200 "$d/index.ts"; done — every one is a bare `export … from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `demo/ui/` wholesale and rewrite its importers to the glass-ui subpaths. The barrels carry no code, so this is a mechanical rename with zero behavioural risk, and it collapses an entire namespace.

defects.defect: `tsconfig.demo.json`'s `paths` map has drifted from `package.json#exports`: three entries point at files that do not exist and two genuinely published subpaths are missing. The Vite half of the same map is machine-generated precisely so it cannot drift; the TS half was left hand-rolled.
defects.evidence: package.json#exports keys = ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize'] (no root). tsconfig.demo.json paths declare `@mkbabb/value.js` → ./dist/index.d.ts, plus /parsing and /units — `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts` → "No such file or directory" ×3. `/value` and `/css` have NO entry though `/css` has 10 demo import sites. vite.config.ts:39-49 generates its alias set from package.json#exports with a comment saying it is generated "so the alias set can never drift". Entering conditional exports. ======== … successfully resolved to '…/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts' with Package ID '…@4.0.0'`.
defects.mechanism: The same map maintained twice — once generated, once by hand. This component's chain crosses it at useMixingState.ts:19 (/color, mapped) and useMixingState.ts:23 → color-session/picker-color → @mkbabb/value.js/css (unmapped, self-referenced).
defects.reproduction: node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports))" vs the paths block in tsconfig.demo.json; then `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts`; then `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit --traceResolution | grep -A4 "@mkbabb/value.js/css"`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `@mkbabb/value.js*` block from tsconfig.demo.json entirely. TypeScript's package self-reference already resolves through the repo's own `exports` map — proved by the trace above — so the map is read from one source instead of mirrored, and the drift surface goes to zero.

defects.defect: This component is unreachable for a first-time visitor, by the same mechanism as L-2: MixSourceSelector.vue:164-176 renders the "Add current color to the mix" control as a `<WatercolorDot tag="button" @click=… aria-label=… :disabled=…>`, and WatercolorDot drops $attrs INCLUDING listeners while hardcoding `pointer-events:none`. Consequence visible in the mega-tranche visual audit: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:123 `/#/mix` text=186 desktop, :153 text=118 mobile, all selector + config bar — no row exercises the result plate.
defects.mechanism: Same as L-2 — the demo codes to a WatercolorDot host seam the published 7.0.0 primitive does not have; here the discarded attrs include the click listener and the pointer-events kill makes even a synthetic click impossible.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/probe-mix-target.mjs — clean chromium profile, no seeded storage, http://localhost:9000/#/mix. Reaching MixResultDisplay at all required seeding localStorage["color-palettes"] with two palettes via addInitScript and using Palettes mode (see L-wbmixresult-probe.mjs).
defects.proposedCure: Same glass-ui repair as L-2 (`as`/`asChild` + `v-bind="$attrs"` + conditional pointer-events). Demo-side interim: the add-slot becomes a real `<button>` that WRAPS a decorative WatercolorDot, so the host element and its semantics belong to the demo and the dot stays a pure paint — which is also exactly the shape L-1's anchor cure requires.

defects.defect: The three <label> elements label nothing; the accessible name arrives from a competing aria-label on the trigger

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant); the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with, declared not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — `variant="primary-audacious"` is not a prop of glass-ui 7.0.0's Button. It falls through Vue's $attrs onto the host `<button>` as a dead HTML attribute, so the pane's ONE verb ships in glass-ui's default `emphasis="secondary"` / `glass-wash glass-capsule` register — precisely the "quiet glass capsule read disabled-forever over the wash tier" that the file's own comment at MixConfigBar.vue:158-161 forbids. Confirmed in the live DOM (`data-emphasis="secondary"`, `variant="primary-audacious"` present as a raw attribute), in glass-ui's built default (`emphasis: { default: "secondary" }`), by grep (the token exists nowhere in glass-ui or demo CSS), and visibly in the captured screenshot. The CI-hard demo typecheck is green (`npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0), so no gate in the repo can see it.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as scoped negative proof so the absences are evidence rather than silence: (1) Full read of all 173 lines — no requestAnimationFrame, no addEventListener, no ResizeObserver/IntersectionObserver, no timers, no lifecycle hooks, no async, no WebGL; the PRM-RAF, leaked-listener and missing-cleanup classes are genuinely absent here. (2) No `defineModel` (explicit defineProps at :32 + defineEmits at :76), so the WritableComputedRef stale-read hazard cannot arise; reactive props destructure at :25-45 is idiomatic Vue 3.5. (3) No `ValueUnit` construction, no `stableHue`, no `parseCssColor` call, no reka slider — the four named local hazards do not touch this file. (4) Boundary sweep: 9 offered spaces x 5 degenerate operand pairs (achromatic, identical, alpha=0, out-of-gamut oklch(1.4 0.9 120)/oklch(-0.2 0.5 300), hue +/-100000) = 45 cases through the real sampler — zero throws, zero NaN/Infinity/undefined stops; `hsl` correctly returns null (honest absence) for achromatic and alpha=0. (5) REPORT.json `/#/mix` rows across all four matrices: consoleErrors [], pageErrors [], overflowX 0. (6) The component contributes ZERO of the measured a11y defects: the 8 small tap targets on /#/mix are all dock/picker (160x23 unnamed input, 22x22 "Switch to slug"/"Generate new slug"/"Cancel", 12x24 L/A/B/ALPHA channel) and the 1 nameless button is `button.send-btn` 24x24 under div.dock-face-content; MixConfigBar's own controls measure 36px triggers, 40px button, 49px menu option rows. (7) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied — all five type-only imports use `import type`; vue-tsc exits 0. (8) No god module, no legacy shim, no invented shared/ dir inside the file.

defects.defect: `variant="primary-audacious"` is not a glass-ui 7.0.0 Button prop; it renders as a dead DOM attribute and the pane's primary verb ships in the default secondary/wash register the file's own comment forbids.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:163. glass-ui ButtonProps (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts) = {emphasis,tone,size,iconOnly,loading,type,disabled,class,asChild,as} — no `variant`. `grep -rn "primary-audacious" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no matches; only 2 demo call sites. Live DOM at localhost:9000/#/mix: attrs include `data-emphasis="secondary"`, class `button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule h-10 …`, and a raw `variant="primary-audacious"`; computed opacity 0.5, bgImage none. glass-ui built default: `emphasis: { default: "secondary" }` (dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js). `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` → `EXIT=0`. Visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png.

If an 'audacious' register is genuinely wanted it is a glass-ui `emphasis` value authored in glass-ui, never a demo-side string (owner edict 4).

defects.defect: In the app's shipped default color space the Hue-method Select is entirely inert and its four preview chips are byte-identical — a preview asserting a distinction that does not exist, which is exactly what the O-14 truth law forbids.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:66-74 samples hueRamps in the CURRENT colorSpace; useMixingState.ts:44 defaults `colorSpace = ref<PickerSpace>("oklab")` (rectangular — mixColors ignores the hue option). Measured via scratch vitest against the real sampler with the component's exact arguments: `OKLAB QUARTET distinct count: 1 of 4`; per-space distinct-arc counts — oklch 2/4, oklab 1/4, lab 1/4, lch 2/4, hsl 2/4, hsv 2/4, hwb 2/4, rgb 1/4, xyz 1/4. Four of the nine offered spaces (color-space-meta.ts:26-36) are rectangular. Default state visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png (COLOR SPACE: OKLab / HUE METHOD: Shorter). The 2/4 result is the mathematical ceiling (shorter always equals one of increasing/decreasing) and is NOT a defect; the 1/4 result is.
defects.mechanism: The component holds `colorSpace` (MixConfigBar.vue:26) and uses it only for sampling — it never gates the hue axis on whether the chosen space has a hue channel, so an inert control renders as live and its preview quartet degenerates.
defects.reproduction: `npx vitest run --config <scratchpad>/vitest.probe.config.ts` with a probe calling `sampleInterpolationRamp(["oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8)","rebeccapurple"], "oklab", m)` for each of the 4 HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS → all four stop lists are string-identical (Set size 1). In the UI: load /#/mix cold (default oklab), add 2 operands, open Hue method → four identical chips.
defects.proposedCure: Add `cylindrical: true` to the five hue-bearing entries of INTERPOLATION_SPACES in the vocabulary module that already owns them (demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts), then bind `:disabled="!isCylindrical(colorSpace)"` on the Hue-method `<Select>` (glass-ui SelectProps.disabled exists) and skip hueRamps entirely in that branch. One fact added once, consumed by both surfaces (Mix and Gradient) that already share the module — no new module, no wrapper.

defects.defect: Both O-14 T-17 chip e2e legs are RED right now, the component has zero unit coverage, and beneath the red the byte-identity assertion cannot match the stamp it claims to compare — so the preview-chip feature has never been verified in a live DOM and can be deleted without changing any gate's colour.
defects.evidence: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o14-preview-truth.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "T-17 chip referent"` → `2 failed, 1 passed (1.3m)`; both failures are `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded … waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Add current color to the mix' })` at spec lines 355 and 414. The one pass asserts chips are ABSENT. Cause: MixSourceSelector.vue:167-171 passes `tag="button"` to WatercolorDot, whose glass-ui 7.0.0 props are exactly {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed} — no `tag`; the failing run's own AX snapshot (test-results/oracles-o14-preview-truth--e0bf9-…/error-context.md:137-142) shows no button in the Selected region. Separately, the spec's parseOklchTriples regex /oklch\(([\d.]+)[ ,]+…/ (spec:162-168) matches 0 of the sampler's real output: node run → "oklch(62% 0.27 9.8deg)" -> [], "oklch(0% 0 none)" -> []; while the browser canonicalizes the paint (measured: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8), …)`) → paintedCount 2 vs stampedCount 0, so `expect(painted.length).toBe(stamped.length)` would be expect(17).toBe(0) per chip. `grep -rn "MixConfigBar" . --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' -l | grep -v node_modules` → only MixPane.vue and a doc comment: no test mounts the component.
defects.mechanism: Same retired-glass-ui-7-prop family as C-1 (`tag` on WatercolorDot) kills the oracle's entry locator; and the oracle's hand-written regex was never validated against the serializer format it parses. Unit coverage tests sample.ts in isolation, never the component's space×hue cross-product wiring.
defects.reproduction: Vacuous-gate mutation: delete both `<PreviewRamp …/>` elements at MixConfigBar.vue:111 and :133. `npm test` stays fully green (nothing imports the component); the one passing e2e leg ('honest absence … the rows carry NO chip') stays green because the chips are now unconditionally absent; the two already-red legs stay red. The entire T-17 feature leaves this component without turning a single gate a different colour.
defects.proposedCure: (1) Fix the add-slot host so the flow is drivable (wb-mix-sourceselector seat). (2) Retire parseOklchTriples: the sampler already owns `stampStops`, so the honest referent is `data-stops.split("|")` compared to the painted stops through ONE shared normalizer — never a hand-written regex duplicating the serializer's grammar. (3) Add a @vue/test-utils mount (already a devDependency) asserting the only logic this file owns: that row i of the Space menu carries the ramp for space i and not for the current space.

defects.defect: Three `<label>` elements label nothing — no `for`, no nested control — so clicking the visible label is inert and the accessible name survives only via a hand-duplicated `aria-label`, while glass-ui's `Label` (with a `for` prop) sits re-exported and unused.

Live DOM measurement: `[{"text":"Color space","htmlFor":"","control":null},{"text":"Hue method","htmlFor":"","control":null},{"text":"Size mismatch","htmlFor":"","control":null}]` — HTMLLabelElement.control === null for all three. Playwright AX snapshot (live, and in the e2e failure context error-context.md:144-148) exposes the text as an orphan `generic` adjacent to the combobox, not as its name. Name duplicated as aria-label at :100, :123, :147. glass-ui exports the primitive and the demo re-exports it: demo/ui/label/index.ts → `export { Label } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` with LabelProps { for?: string; requirement?; disabled? }.
defects.mechanism: Hand-rolled bare `<label class="section-label">` instead of the design system's own labeled-control primitive — a design-system bypass that produces an HTML-invalid dangling label and forces the name to be authored twice.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('label.section-label')].map(l=>({t:l.textContent.trim(), for:l.htmlFor, control:l.control}))` → all three have `for: ""` and `control: null`. Clicking the visible 'Color space' text does not focus or open the Select.
defects.proposedCure: `<Label for="mix-space">Color space</Label>` + `id="mix-space"` on the trigger (×3), and drop the duplicated `aria-label`s. One name, authored once, in the design system's own primitive (owner edict 4).

defects.defect: `class="h-9"` on all three SelectTriggers drops glass-ui's token-driven height class and hardcodes a per-instance pixel height that equals the design system's existing `size="sm"` register exactly.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:100, :123, :147. glass-ui computes the trigger height from a token (dist/select-BcBAyLXA.js:98-101): `case "sm": return "h-(--control-h-sm)"; default: return "h-(--control-h-md)"` and merges consumer class through tailwind-merge. Measured live: rendered `triggerClass` ends `… transition-control … h-9` with NO `h-(--control-h-*)` token class present; `triggerHeight: "36px"`; tokens `--control-h-sm: max(calc(2.25rem * 1), 0px)` = 36px, `--control-h-md: max(calc(2.5rem * 1), 0px)` = 40px. h-9 = 2.25rem = 36px = exactly --control-h-sm.
defects.mechanism: Per-instance class costume over a root-level register the design system already parameterizes (owner edict 5) — severs three controls from the token, so a future retune of --control-h-sm moves every control in the app except these.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/mix and evaluate `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[aria-label="Color space"]')).height` → "36px", and read `.className` → contains `h-9`, contains no `h-(--control-h-` token class.

defects.defect: The decorative `<Blend>` icon carries no `aria-hidden`, so it is exposed as a nameless `img` node inside the Mix button.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:168 `<Blend class="w-4 h-4" />`; @lucide/vue does not set aria-hidden. Measured AX tree (e2e error-context.md:155-157): `button "Mix" [disabled]: - img - text: Mix`. The sibling component does it right — MixSourceSelector.vue:174 `<Plus class="w-5 h-5 …" aria-hidden="true" />`.
defects.mechanism: Missing decorative-icon suppression; an inconsistency inside the same feature, not a house style.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/mix, take a Playwright AX snapshot of the Mix button → a bare `img` child node with no accessible name.
defects.proposedCure: `<Blend class="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />`.

defects.defect: The component reaches past the design system into `reka-ui` for `AcceptableValue` — a type wider than glass-ui's actual emit — then launders it into the domain type with three unchecked `as` casts.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:15 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui";` and handlers at :99, :122, :146 of the form `(v: AcceptableValue) => emit('update:colorSpace', v as PickerSpace)`. glass-ui 7.0.0's contract is narrower: `SelectEmits { "update:modelValue": [value: SelectionValue] }` with `export type SelectionValue = string | number` (dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts). reka's AcceptableValue includes `Record<string,any> | null`. `reka-ui` is a devDependency (package.json). Four demo components carry the same reach (GradientVisualizer.vue:28, GenerateControls.vue:33, AuroraPane.vue:25, this file).
defects.mechanism: Design-system bypass plus a masking cast (owner edict 2: no masking fallbacks) — the handler advertises values glass-ui will never send and `as` erases the narrowing obligation.
defects.reproduction: Read node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts (`SelectionValue = string | number`) against MixConfigBar.vue:99. The cast compiles for `null`, which is in AcceptableValue and not in PickerSpace.
defects.proposedCure: Annotate `(v: string | number)` — literally SelectionValue — and narrow honestly with a membership check against INTERPOLATION_SPACES / HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS (both already imported and already the source of the rendered rows) instead of `as`. That also closes C-11. Deleting the reka-ui import from the demo tree is the architectural half.

defects.defect: The leftover-strategy vocabulary is duplicated inside the view as a non-exhaustive array, against the precept the file itself cites eight lines earlier for the interpolation vocabulary.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:83-89: `const STRATEGIES: LeftoverStrategy[] = ["discard","repeat","distribute"]` plus a `Record<LeftoverStrategy,string>`. The type is owned by demo/palettes/mix.ts:19. The Record is exhaustiveness-checked by TypeScript; the array is not — adding a fourth member to the union compiles clean and the new strategy silently never appears in the menu. MixConfigBar.vue:16-18 states the opposite principle for the other vocabulary ("the interpolation vocabulary lives in its neutral @lib/ home … no more cross-feature reach").
defects.mechanism: Vocabulary left behind in the consumer instead of beside the type that owns it, producing a hand-maintained parallel list with no exhaustiveness guarantee.
defects.reproduction: Add a 4th member to `LeftoverStrategy` in demo/palettes/mix.ts:19 → `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` fails on `strategyLabels` (good) but STRATEGIES is silently short by one, so the row never renders.
defects.proposedCure: Move label+value metadata beside the type in demo/palettes/mix.ts using the same shape color-space-meta.ts already uses, and import it. Zero new modules — the neutral home already exists.

defects.defect: The pane's only verb is natively `disabled` on every cold load with no stated reason and no tab reach, and the asynchronous mix result is never announced.
defects.evidence: Measured live: `{"disabled": true, "ariaDisabled": null, "opacity": "0.5"}`. MixConfigBar.vue:164 `:disabled="!canMix"`; canMix requires >=2 selections (useMixingState.ts:50-53), which is false on every cold /#/mix load. No aria-describedby, no hint text anywhere on the pane. The result lands in MixResultDisplay via MixPane.vue:111-119 with no aria-live / role=status in the chain. Combined with the C-1 wash register the button is the faintest element in shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png.
defects.mechanism: Disabled-state and async-result accessibility never authored: a native `disabled` button is removed from the tab order, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot reach it to discover why it is unavailable.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix cold and Tab through the pane — the Mix button is never focused; evaluate `btn.getAttribute('aria-disabled')` → null. Complete a mix and observe no live-region announcement.
defects.proposedCure: Keep the button focusable and use `aria-disabled` plus a short `aria-describedby` hint on the disabled state, and give the result plate `role="status"` (that half belongs to the result surface — noted so it is not dropped between components).

defects.defect: The parent recreates `operandColors` as a new array on every render, so both ramp computeds invalidate on renders where nothing changed by value, forcing a full ~0.5 ms resample of all rows while a menu is open.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:103 `:operand-colors="mode === 'colors' ? selectedColors.map((sc) => sc.css) : []"` — a fresh array identity per parent render, so Vue's Object.is prop check always reports changed. Measured full recompute of both maps (9 spaces + 4 arcs, RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT = 16): operands=2 → 0.638 ms, operands=3 → 0.506 ms, operands=5 → 0.512 ms. The file's own 'costs nothing at rest' claim (MixConfigBar.vue:19-22) is otherwise TRUE — computeds are lazy and SelectContent unmounts closed (verified: 9 option rows, chips 0 each, with <2 operands; the one green e2e leg finds 0 [data-stops] closed).
defects.mechanism: Unstable prop identity from an inline template expression in the parent; sub-frame cost, so no user-visible consequence was measured.
defects.reproduction: `npx vitest run --config <scratchpad>/vitest.probe.config.ts` PROBE C times 50 reps of INTERPOLATION_SPACES.forEach(sampleInterpolationRamp) + HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS.forEach(sampleInterpolationRamp) → 0.506–0.638 ms per full recompute.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist to a `computed` in MixPane so the array identity is stable while the selection is unchanged.

defects.defect: `<SelectValue />` carries no placeholder while the prop's type (PickerSpace = SpaceId, 17 members) is a strict superset of the 9 spaces the menu offers — a value outside the 9 renders a blank trigger with no fallback text.
defects.evidence: MixConfigBar.vue:101 `<SelectValue />` (SelectValueProps.placeholder exists per dist/components/select/SelectValue.vue.d.ts). demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:35 `export type PickerSpace = SpaceId` — the full library union (rgb,hsl,hsv,hwb,lab,lch,oklab,oklch,xyz,kelvin,ictcp,jzazbz,prophotoRgb,rec2020,a98Rgb,displayP3,linearSrgb). INTERPOLATION_SPACES (color-space-meta.ts:26-36) lists 9.
defects.mechanism: Prop type wider than the rendered vocabulary, with no placeholder to absorb the gap.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a HYPOTHESIS on reachability. colorSpace is a ref local to useMixingState and only this Select writes it, so no live path sets an unlisted space today. The type hole is factual; it becomes live the moment mix state is lifted, URL-persisted, or shared with the picker's 17-space catalog.
defects.proposedCure: Closed structurally by the C-7 cure (narrow with a membership check against INTERPOLATION_SPACES instead of `as PickerSpace`); add a placeholder as belt-and-braces.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited)
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the plate's advertised convergence anchor `[data-mix-target]` (MixResultDisplay.vue:69) never reaches the DOM, because glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot is `inheritAttrs:false` and binds only `attrs.class`/`attrs.style`; measured `document.querySelectorAll('main [data-mix-target]').length === 0` at all 16 sampled frames of a live mix, and `mixStage.ts:121-124` silently falls back to a geometric guess (`root.clientWidth/2, root.scrollHeight*0.7, r:28`). The component's entire design premise — "the DESTINATION the convergence lands on" — is unrealised in the shipped build, and a masking fallback hides it.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Two candidate findings were withdrawn after disproof: a "plate spontaneously disappears" claim traced to my own stray click plus a concurrent seat navigating the shared dev page, and a "one-stop linear-gradient is invalid CSS" claim disproved by measuring getComputedStyle(...).backgroundImage === "linear-gradient(to right, rgb(255, 0, 0))".)

defects.defect: The announced convergence anchor `[data-mix-target]` does not exist in the DOM; a silent geometric fallback masks it, so the plate is never the destination it advertises.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:69 sets `data-mix-target` on <WatercolorDot>. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js: `inheritAttrs: !1` and the render binds only `c = i(() => n.class)` / `f = i(() => n.style)` onto a hardcoded `<span aria-hidden="true" data-testid="watercolor-swatch" data-variant=… pointerEvents:"none">`. Live probe over a full mix (16 samples, before→+2000ms): `document.querySelectorAll('main [data-mix-target]').length === 0` at EVERY frame. Fallback: demo/workbenches/mix/MixAnimationCanvas/composables/mixStage.ts:121-124 `targetEl ? layoutCenter(targetEl, root) : { x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7, r: 28 }`.
defects.mechanism: consumer identity/semantics attached as fallthrough attributes to a producer component that discards everything except class and style; a masking fallback converts the resulting breakage into plausible-looking motion
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix → Palettes tab → select two palettes → Mix. During and after the narration, `document.querySelectorAll('main [data-mix-target]').length` is 0.
defects.proposedCure: Identity belongs to markup the consumer owns: wrap the ghost dot in a real `<div data-mix-target>` (or a named seat primitive), and delete the fallback in collectStage so a missing anchor returns null and fails loudly. Re-audit every WatercolorDot call site against the 7.0.0 prop set — MixSourceSelector's add-slot is dead by the same mechanism (its aria-label, @click and tag="button" are all dropped; the rendered node is an aria-hidden, pointer-events:none span, which is the nameless button REPORT.md:99,106 records on /#/mix).

defects.defect: A palette result carries no readable truth: no visible values, no titles, no accessible names, and every swatch is producer-forced `aria-hidden`.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:103 `:title="color.css"` — dropped by the producer (measured on the settled 3-colour plate: `dots: [{ariaHidden:"true", title:null, tag:null, w:40} ×3]`). Only the single-colour branch prints a value (lines 85-87). Measured `plate.innerText === "RESULT"`. Frames: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-resultdisplay/frames/plate-settled-palette-{light,dark}.png. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.2 ("data-bearing static faces remain present as noninteractive NAMED list/text content") and §4.1; PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07.
defects.mechanism: the plural case's only truth channel is a tooltip attribute on a component that cannot receive attributes; no text representation was ever designed for palette results
defects.reproduction: /#/mix → Palettes → select two → Mix → the settled plate contains exactly one text node, 'Result'; all three swatch spans have title=null and aria-hidden=true.
defects.proposedCure: Render the palette branch as named data: ordinal + value in `text-mono-small` rows (the type role the single-colour branch already uses), with the dots demoted to decoration beside the data rather than the sole carrier of it.

defects.defect: The declared 'one surface, new content' morph is measurably a 68px collapse-and-reopen, shows the STALE previous result for the first ~400ms, and lands 400ms after the clock declares done.
defects.evidence: Measured `.mix-plate` rect over one live mix: before h=167.8 top=706.1 (3 dots); +16→+200 h=167.8 with ghost class true, opacity 1→0.55, still 3 dots of the PREVIOUS result; +400→+800 h=99.8 top=713.1, 1 dot; +900 ghost class removed, still h=99.8; +1300 h=167.8, 3 dots. Δh = ±68.0px (±68%), Δtop = 7px, un-animated: `--vj-morph-collapse`/`--vj-morph-expanded` are never set so animations.css:104-136's max-height arm resolves none→none. Final content at ~1300ms vs the "Total wall clock ≤ 1.2 s" contract in useMixingAnimation.ts:21-22. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 forbids the "full-slab remount hole".
defects.mechanism: `mode="out-in"` on a surface whose two arms have different intrinsic heights, with the family's height-morph variables left unset
defects.reproduction: /#/mix with a palette result already on screen → press Mix again → sample `.mix-plate` getBoundingClientRect().height at t+16/+400/+1300ms → 167.8 / 99.8 / 167.8.
defects.proposedCure: Make the ghost the result's shape (D-8) so settle is an ink-in at constant geometry; keep one surface with keyed content and no out-in; if a height morph is genuinely wanted, set the --vj-morph-collapse/-expanded the family already exposes rather than shipping an inert transition.

defects.defect: The plate's only identity line renders at 2.21:1 contrast for the entire ~900ms mixing window, because reduced presence is applied to the whole container instead of the specimen.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:155-157 `.mix-plate--ghost { opacity: 0.55 }`. Measured (canvas-resolved sRGB, WCAG 2.x): label rgb(112,89,66) on plate rgb(233,225,217) = 5.08:1 settled; composited at 0.55 alpha = 2.21:1 — below the 4.5:1 AA text floor and below the 3:1 non-text floor. Ghost class measured present from +16ms to ~+900ms. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: "Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence."
defects.mechanism: presence attenuation at the container tier rather than the specimen tier
defects.reproduction: /#/mix → Palettes → two palettes → Mix; during the ghost window read getComputedStyle('.mix-plate').opacity === '0.55' and composite the label colour against the plate background — 2.21:1.
defects.proposedCure: Attenuate only the well and the seeded silhouette (the §2 'Watercolor/data' specimen lane). The identity line never dims — it is the one element that explains the reduced-presence state.

defects.defect: Three unlabeled 28×28px icon actions that explicitly opt out of the producer's 44px standalone touch floor via `compact`, with `title` doing double duty as name AND state.
defects.evidence: Measured: all three DockControls 28×28 CSS px, aria-label=null, innerText=""; only name is `title`. MixResultDisplay.vue:122,129,137 pass `compact`. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/controls/touch-floor.css: `@media (pointer: coarse) { .dock-icon-button:not(.dock-icon-button--compact):not(:where(.glass-dock *)) { min-block-size: var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem); min-inline-size: var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem) } }` — compact is carved out and the plate is not inside a .glass-dock. Line 123 `:title="copied ? 'Copied!' : 'Copy color'"` carries state in the name. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 7; PR-07. Honest scope: 28px clears WCAG 2.5.8 (AA 24px) and the harness probe (capture.mjs:87) and fails WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA 44px) and the producer's own floor.
defects.mechanism: choosing the producer's compact variant trades away the hit-box≠paint-box affordance the same producer ships for standalone controls
defects.reproduction: /#/mix with a settled result → measure the three buttons in `.mix-plate`: 28×28 each, aria-label null.
defects.proposedCure: Drop `compact`; give each control a real accessible name; leave `title` as a tooltip only, never as the name or the state channel.

defects.defect: The 'Result' label hand-rolls a per-instance approximation of the producer's `.section-label` in the wrong family and weight, contradicting its own sibling label 200px away in the same pane.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:58 `font-display text-caption font-bold text-muted-foreground uppercase tracking-wide` → measured computed: Fraunces / 700 / 12.179px / letter-spacing 0.304px. MixConfigBar.vue:98 `.section-label` → measured computed: "Fira Code" / 400 / 12.179px / letter-spacing 1.218px. Producer rule: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/utilities.css `.section-label { @apply text-mono-caption; color: var(--muted-foreground) }`. A third spelling for the same job at MixSourceSelector.vue:119. `.section-label` is used 20× across 9 demo files. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 closes the type matrix (label = text-small, PJS, non-bold; Fraunces owns display/identity); PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 13; owner edicts 4 and 5.
defects.mechanism: per-instance utility stack re-creating a root-level producer recipe, and getting family/weight/tracking wrong in the process
defects.reproduction: /#/mix settled → getComputedStyle on `.mix-plate > span` vs `.section-label`: Fraunces/700/0.304px vs Fira Code/400/1.218px.
defects.proposedCure: `Result`, then normalise MixSourceSelector's 'Selected' to the same recipe so the Mix composition has one label species instead of three.

defects.defect: The decorative gradient strip restates the specimen at 3.16× its inline extent and contradicts it about palette order in RTL.
defects.evidence: Measured on the settled 3-colour plate: swatch row inline extent 430px, swatch ink 136px (fill ratio 0.316); strip 430×16px. RTL probe with document.documentElement.dir toggled: dots move to x=425/377/329 (colors[0] rightmost) while getComputedStyle(strip).backgroundImage stays `linear-gradient(to right, colors[0], colors[1], colors[2])` — the row mirrors, the strip does not, so the two representations of one ordered palette disagree. MixResultDisplay.vue:107-116 (comment literally says 'decorative'). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1 (palette/release order preserves explicit ordinal identity), §3 law 8; PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 laws 5-6.
defects.mechanism: a physical CSS direction keyword painting ordered data whose sibling representation follows logical document direction
defects.reproduction: /#/mix with a palette result → record dot x-positions and the strip's computed background-image in LTR, then set document.documentElement.dir='rtl' and record again: dots reverse, gradient does not.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the strip — it is self-declared decoration duplicating the swatch row exactly, and subtraction precedes explanation. If a continuous reading is genuinely wanted it becomes THE representation, painted `to inline-end`, with the dots demoted to named data rows.

defects.defect: The ghost announces a single 40px well for an N-colour palette result, so the 'silhouette the pigment poured into is the silhouette the result wears' claim is false for every palette mix.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:63-73 renders exactly one WatercolorDot, `:class="result.type === 'color' ? 'w-14 h-14' : 'w-10 h-10'"`; wellColor (lines 36-40) paints `colors[0]` and drops the rest. Measured: ghost frame dots=1, settled frame dots=3. Docstring claim at lines 15-17. The count is knowable before the narration: the result is computed synchronously at startMix (useMixingState.ts:85-98).
defects.mechanism: the announced destination models only the singular case; the plural case is discovered at settle
defects.reproduction: /#/mix → Palettes → two palettes → Mix → count `[data-testid="watercolor-swatch"]` inside `.mix-plate` during the ghost window (1) and after settle (3).
defects.proposedCure: The ghost renders N wells with the N result seeds so settle is an ink-in at constant geometry — which retires D-3's height pump as a side effect.

defects.defect: Copy exists twice in the Mix instrument with divergent feedback and duplicated serialization logic, and neither path renders the producer's `failure` state.
defects.evidence: Plate: MixResultDisplay.vue:31-32,42-47 (`useClipboard({resetMs:1500})`, icon+title swap). Dock: usePaneRouter.ts:222 `{key:'copy', title:'Copy result'}` → MixPane.vue:49-55 (bare `writeClipboard`, `{ok}` discarded, no feedback). Serialization duplicated verbatim: MixResultDisplay.vue:43-46 vs MixPane.vue:51-53. useClipboard.d.ts:3 declares `ClipboardStatus = "idle"|"pending"|"success"|"failure"` plus onCopyError/invalidate; line 32 maps only `success`, so a failed copy is pixel-identical to idle. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-13 and PR-06 (one action owner across Generate/owner/Admin/Mix); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.
defects.mechanism: two owners for one verb, each consuming a different arm of the same producer composable; the producer's failure arm discarded by both
defects.reproduction: Read usePaneRouter.ts:222 + MixPane.vue:49-55 against MixResultDisplay.vue:42-47 — two independent Copy handlers for the same payload with different feedback. (The stale-confirmation consequence of the unused `invalidate()` is a HYPOTHESIS: I did not land a live repro before a concurrent seat navigated the shared page.)
defects.proposedCure: One owner: the plate owns the action, the dock entry delegates to the same handler or is deleted. Render a named failure state, and call `invalidate()` whenever `result` changes so a confirmation can never outlive its payload.

defects.defect: Save is a silent, unbounded, unconfirmed write — no status, no name, no duplicate guard, no undo.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:131 `emit('save')` → MixPane.vue:38-47 `pm.createPalette("Mixed Color"|"Mixed Palette", …)`. Measured: the settled plate contains no status node whatsoever (`plate.innerText === "RESULT"`); the plate has no error/pending/success region in its template at all. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 ("Pending/failure/export/recovery truth only transient → ADD-AFFORDANCE. Persistent entity status/recovery"); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 ("a transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth").
defects.mechanism: a persistent entity mutation wired as a fire-and-forget emit, with the durable truth living only in another route
defects.reproduction: /#/mix with a settled result → press Save repeatedly → the plate never changes; N identically named palettes are created.
defects.proposedCure: Save resolves to a durable statement inside the plate (named entity + link) and is idempotent per result, or it moves into the library flow that already owns naming and lifecycle.

defects.defect: A `role="separator"` that paints nothing: announced to AT, invisible on screen, with contradictory orientation attributes.
defects.evidence: Measured on the live action row: DockSeparator renders 1 × 0 px, `aria-orientation="vertical"` with `data-orientation="horizontal"`; background color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.15) over zero height. MixResultDisplay.vue:135. It is inside a plain `flex items-center` row, not a .glass-dock, so nothing stretches it. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 (every non-Admin divider is zero) and §5 law 4; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 (AT and visual channels must agree).
defects.mechanism: a dock-context primitive used outside its dock, where its cross-axis paint has no source of extent
defects.reproduction: /#/mix settled → `document.querySelector('.mix-plate [role="separator"]').getBoundingClientRect()` → {width:1, height:0}.
defects.proposedCure: Delete it. Three controls in one region need no group boundary.

defects.defect: One 12px interval for four different structural relations: no title gap, no section gap, no hierarchy.
defects.evidence: Measured: `.mix-plate { gap: 12px; padding: 16px }` and the inner column also `gap: 12px`. Identity(18.7px line box)→content(108px block), specimen→decoration and decoration→actions all sit at 12px. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 3: "Header→headline uses title gap; headline→next semantic section uses section gap."
defects.mechanism: a single Tailwind gap utility standing in for two distinct semantic intervals
defects.reproduction: /#/mix settled → getComputedStyle('.mix-plate').gap === '12px' and the same on its content column.
defects.proposedCure: Distinguish the title gap from the section gap using the producer's instrument tokens, so the identity line reads as an identity line rather than an eyebrow.

defects.defect: Truthiness guards leave an empty palette result and a css-less colour result rendering half-plates that were never designed.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:91 `v-if="result.type === 'palette' && result.colors"` — `[]` is truthy; demo/palettes/mix.ts:112-121 returns `[]` for `palettes.length === 0` and for `resultLength === 0`. Line 78 `v-if="result.type === 'color' && result.css"` — a falsy css yields a plate with a label and an action row and no specimen. Neither arm has designed empty/error styling.
defects.mechanism: array-truthiness used as a presence guard; no designed empty/failed arm in a component whose upstream can return empty
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis. It requires a stored palette with zero colours, which I did not construct. The code path and the JS truthiness are facts; reachability is unproven.
defects.proposedCure: Guard on `colors?.length`, and add one designed arm that names why there is no result rather than rendering a decorated blank.

defects.defect: `:key="i"` makes the wrapping TransitionGroup structurally inert for the only case that matters — re-mixing.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:92-106: `<TransitionGroup name="vj-enter">` over `v-for="(color, i) in result.colors" :key="i"`. Index keys mean an equal-length re-mix emits no enter, no leave and no `vj-enter-move` (animations.css:99-101). The sibling file solves exactly this with a stable key map — MixSourceSelector.vue:76-93, commented "Stable keys for TransitionGroup".
defects.mechanism: positional keys on a keyed-transition primitive whose entire contract is item identity
defects.reproduction: /#/mix with a palette result → change Color space → Mix again: the dots' colours mutate in place with no enter/leave/move transition despite the declared name.
defects.proposedCure: Key on colour identity (or reuse the sibling's stable key map), or drop the TransitionGroup and stop declaring motion that cannot run.

defects.defect: Dead props, redundant producer-owned attributes and an unnecessary import — none of which the typecheck gate can see.
defects.evidence: `tag="div"` at MixResultDisplay.vue:67,81,100 is not a prop of glass-ui 7's WatercolorDot (prop set: color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed) and is dropped — measured `tag === null` on every live dot. `aria-hidden="true"` (line 72) duplicates a producer-hardcoded attribute and is also dropped. `TransitionGroup` is imported (line 4) while `Transition` is not (line 60), proving the import is unnecessary. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
defects.mechanism: markup written against a superseded producer API, kept alive by a template checker that treats unknown attributes as fallthrough
defects.reproduction: Run `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0 while `tag="div"` resolves to nothing in the rendered DOM.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the dead props and the redundant aria-hidden and the unused import; add a call-site sweep (or a lint rule) that fails on props absent from a producer's declared prop set, since the type gate structurally cannot.

defects.defect: The component appears in zero of the megatranche's 60 visual captures, so no π/DELTA claim about it can cite the matrix.
defects.evidence: MixPane.vue:112 `v-if="mixResult"`; all 60 captures in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md are at-rest route loads. I read shots/safari-desktop-light/mix.png and shots/safari-mobile-dark/mix.png: both show Mix at rest with no Result plate. The /#/mix rows (REPORT.md:123,138,153,168) therefore measure a pane that never produced a result.
defects.mechanism: a conditional component excluded by an at-rest-only capture matrix
defects.reproduction: Open the two shots above — neither contains the plate; the REPORT rows for /#/mix carry text lengths of 186 (desktop) and 118 (mobile), consistent with the at-rest pane only.
defects.proposedCure: audit/visual/states.mjs must drive Mix to `done` and capture both the ghost and the settled plate across light/dark and desktop/mobile.

defects.defect: The CSS value artifact is neither LTR-isolated (canon letter) nor wrapped at token boundaries.
defects.evidence: MixResultDisplay.vue:85-87 `{{ result.css }}` — no dir="ltr", no unicode-bidi isolation, against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1 ("CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose"). Measured honestly: for `oklab(0.6 0.1 0.05)` under dir=rtl the glyph order did NOT change (o@36.3, (@79.4, )@191.4 rtl vs o@0, (@43.1, )@155.1 ltr) — the letter of the law is unmet while this string form renders intact. Separately `break-all` splits a colour literal mid-number.
defects.mechanism: a code artifact rendered as ordinary inline prose
defects.reproduction: Range-measure the glyph x-positions of the value span under dir=ltr and dir=rtl (numbers above): no reordering for this string form; the missing isolation is a canon-letter violation, not a rendering defect here.
defects.proposedCure: Wrap the value in an LTR-isolated span and use `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on a `min-width:0` flex child instead of `break-all`, so the artifact wraps at token boundaries.
